By the universal property of $C(G\wr_{*,\beta}{\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi))$, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\varphi\,:\,C(G\wr_{*,\beta}{\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi))\rightarrow C(G\wr_{*}{\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi))$ such that $\varphi\vert_{C({\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi))}=\iota_B$ and  $({\rm id}\otimes\varphi)\rho=\varphi_0$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
\label{RemarkNewExample} If $\Lambda$ is abelian then we have a canonical isomorphism $\widehat{\Gamma}\wr_{*,\beta}\widehat{\Lambda}\simeq \widehat{\Gamma}^{*\Lambda}\rtimes\Lambda$, where the action $\Lambda\curvearrowright\Lambda$ is by left multiplication. Indeed, by Proposition \ref{PropSemiDirect} and Remark \ref{RmkFwp} $(5)$, it suffices to show that the two actions $\Lambda\curvearrowright \mathbb{C}^\Lambda=C(\Lambda)$ and $\widehat{\Lambda}\curvearrowright C^*(\Lambda)=C(\widehat{\Lambda})$ are isomorphic and it follows from the self Pontryagin's duality of finite abelian groups.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{PropFreeProdAction}
Let $I$ be a finite set and for all $i\in I$, $B_i$ a finite dimensional C*-algebra. Consider the unital C*-algebra $B:=\bigoplus B_i$ with canonical surjections $\chi_i\,:\, B\rightarrow B_i$. Suppose that $\beta_i\,:\, B_i\rightarrow B_i\otimes C(H_i)$ is an action, for all $i\in I$. Let $H$ be a CQG containing all the $H_i$ as dual quantum subgroups. Then, there exists a unique action $\beta\,:\, B\rightarrow B\otimes C(H)$ such that, viewing $C(H_i)\subset C(H)$ one has, for all $i\in I$, $\beta_i\circ\chi_i=(\chi_i\otimes{\rm id})\beta$. Moreover, if all the $\beta_i$ are $\psi_i$-preserving for some state $\psi\in B_i^*$ then, $\beta$ is $\psi$-preserving for $\psi:=\vert I\vert^{-1}\sum_{i\in I}\psi_i\circ\chi_i$.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
View $\beta_i\circ\chi_i\,:\, B\rightarrow B_i\otimes C(H_i)\subset B_i\otimes C(H)$. By the universal property of direct sum there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\beta\,:\, B\rightarrow B\otimes C(H)$ such that $(\chi_i\otimes{\rm id})\beta=\beta_i\circ\chi_i$. Since $H_i$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $H$ one has, for all $i\in I$, \begin{eqnarray*}
(\chi_i\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_H)\beta&=&({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_H)\beta_i\circ\chi_i=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{H_i})\beta_i=(\beta_i\otimes{\rm id})\beta_i\circ\chi_i\\
&=&(\beta_i\circ\chi_i\otimes{\rm id})\beta=(\chi_i\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta\otimes{\rm id})\beta
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_H)\beta=(\beta\otimes{\rm id})\beta$. Note that $(\chi_i\otimes\varepsilon_H)\beta=({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_H)\beta_i\circ\chi_i=({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_{H_i})\beta_i\circ\chi_i=\chi_i(\cdot)1$ for all $i\in I$. Hence, $({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_H)\beta={\rm id}_B$ and $\beta$ is an action. The uniqueness and the last statement are clear.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{ExErgoDec}
Let $\beta_B\,:\,{\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi)\curvearrowright B$ be the universal action and assume that $\psi$ is not a $\delta$-form. Write the ergodic decomposition decomposition $(B,\psi)=\bigoplus (B_i,\psi_i)$. Brannan's result precisely means that ${\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi)=\underset{i\in I}{*}{\rm Aut}^+(B_i, \psi_i)$ and $\beta_B$ is the action associated with the universal actions $\beta_{B_i}\,:\,{\rm Aut}^+(B_i, \psi_i)\curvearrowright B_i$.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{deltafree}
For each $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$ let $B_p$ be a finite dimensional C*-algebra with a faithful state $\psi_p\in B_p^*$ and $\beta_p\,:\,H_p\curvearrowright B_p$ be a $\psi_p$-preserving action. Let $(B,\psi):=\bigoplus_{p\in V(\mathcal{G})}(B_p,\psi_p)$ with the associated $\psi$-preserving action $\beta\,:\,H\curvearrowright B$. Then, for any compact quantum group $G$ with dual quantum subgroup $F$, there is a canonical isomorphism $$G\wr_{*,\beta,F}H\simeq\pi_1(G\wr_{*,\beta_p,F}H_p,\Sigma_e\times F,\mathcal{G},\mathcal{T}),$$
where the graph maps on the right are given by
$$s'_e:=s_e\otimes{\rm id}\,:\,C(\Sigma_e\times F)\rightarrow C(H_{s(e)}\times F)\subset C(G\wr_{*,\beta_{s(e)},F}H_{s(e)}),$$
which clearly intertwines the comultiplications.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Write $C(H)=\langle C(H_p),u_e\vert p\in V(\mathcal{G}),\,e\in E(\mathcal{G})\rangle$. Let $\mathbb{G}:=G\wr_{*,\beta,F}H$, $\mathbb{G}_p:=G\wr_{*,\beta_p,F}H_p$ with canonical homomorphisms $\rho\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and $\rho_p\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B_p\otimes C(\mathbb{G}_p)$ and view $C(H\times F)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$ and $C(H_p\times F)\subset C(\mathbb{G}_p)$. Define $\mathbb{G}':=\pi_1(\mathbb{G}_p,\Sigma_e\times F,\mathcal{G},\mathcal{T})$ and write $C(\mathbb{G}')=\langle C(\mathbb{G}_p), v_e\vert p\in V(\mathcal{G}),\,e\in E(\mathcal{G})\rangle$. Note that, for all $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$ and $b\in C(\Sigma_e)$ one has, viewing $C(\Sigma_e)\subset C(\Sigma_e\times F)$, $r'_e(b)=v_{\overline{e}}(s'_e(b))v_e$. By the universal property of $C(H)$ there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\nu_{H}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')$ such that $\nu_{H}(u_e)=v_e$ and $\nu_{H}\vert_{C(H_p)}$ is the inclusion $C(H_p)\subset C(\mathbb{G}_p)\subset C(\mathbb{G}')$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Note that, by definition, all the maps $s_e'\vert_{C(F)}\,:\, C(F)\subset C(\Sigma_e\times F)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}_{s(e)})\subset C(\mathbb{G}')$ coincide, for $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. Write $\nu_F\,:\, C(F)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')$ the unique map such that $\nu_F=s_e'\vert_{C(F)}$ for all $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. The fundamental quantum group relations give, for all $f\in C(F)$ and $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$,
$$\nu_F(f)=s'_{\overline{e}}(f)=r'_e(f)=v_{\overline{e}}(s'_e(f))v_e=v_e^*\nu_F(f)v_e.$$
Hence, $\nu_F(C(F))$ commutes with $v_e$ for all $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. Also, by the free wreath product relations, $C(F)\subset C(\mathbb{G}_p)$ and $C(H_p)\subset C(\mathbb{G}_p)$ commute, for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$. Hence, $\nu_F(C(F))$ commutes with the C*-algebra generated by $C(H_p)$, $p\in V(G)$ and $v_e$, $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$ inside $C(\mathbb{G}')$. This C*-algebra is exactly $\nu_H(C(H))$ so we have the relation $[\nu_H(x),\nu_F(f)]=0$ for all $a\in C(H)$ and $f\in C(F)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Viewing $C(\mathbb{G}_p)\subset C(\mathbb{G}')$, we may view each map $\rho_p$ as a map $ C(G)\rightarrow B_p\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')$. By universal property of the direct sum there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\rho'\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')$ such that $(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})\rho'=\rho_p$ for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$, where $\chi_p\,:\, B\rightarrow B_p$ is the canonical surjection. Note that, for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})[\rho'(a)({\rm id}\otimes\nu_{H})(\beta(b))]&=&\rho_p(a)({\rm id}\otimes\nu_{H})(\beta_p(\chi_p(b)))=\rho_p(a)\beta_p(\chi_p(b))\\
&=&\beta_p(\chi_p(b))\rho_p(a)
=(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})[({\rm id}\otimes\nu_{H})(\beta(b))\rho'(a)].\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, $[\rho'(a),({\rm id}\otimes\nu_{H})(\beta(b))]=0$ for all $a\in C(G)$, $b\in B$. Moreover, $$(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})\rho'(f)=\rho_p(f)=1_{B_p}\otimes f\text{ for all }f\in C(F).$$
Hence, $\rho'(f)=1_{B}\otimes f$ for all $f\in C(F)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent By the universal property of $C(\mathbb{G})$, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism
$$\pi\,:\, C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')\text{ such that }({\rm id}\otimes\pi)\rho=\rho'\text{ and }\pi\vert_{C(H)}=\nu_H,\,\, \pi\vert_{C(F)}=\nu_F.$$
Consider now the canonical maps:
$$\beta_G\,:\, C(G)\otimes B\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G})\text{ and }\beta^p_{G}\,:\,C(G)\otimes B_p\rightarrow B_p\otimes C(\mathbb{G}_p).$$
We claim that:
\begin{equation}\label{EqBetaG}
(\chi_p\otimes\pi)\beta_G=\beta_G^p({\rm id}\otimes\chi_p)\quad\text{for all }p\in V(\mathcal{G})
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $a\in C(G)$ and $b\in B$ one has,
\begin{eqnarray*}
(\chi_p\otimes\pi)\beta_G(a\otimes b)&=&(\chi_p\otimes\pi)(\rho(a)\beta(b))=(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})(\rho'(a))({\rm id}\otimes\pi)(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})(\beta(b))\\
&=&\rho_p(a)\beta_p(\chi_p(b))=\beta^p_G(a\otimes\chi_p(b)).
\end{eqnarray*}
Let us show that $\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}\circ\pi=(\pi\otimes\pi)\circ\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}$. Since $\nu_H \,:\, C(H)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')$ intertwines the comultiplications and $H$ is a dual subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, it suffices to show that
$$({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'})({\rm id}\otimes\pi)\rho=({\rm id}\otimes\pi\otimes\pi)({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_\mathbb{G})\rho.$$
Using Equation $(\ref{EqBetaG})$ we find, for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
(\chi_p\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'})({\rm id}\otimes\pi)\rho&=&(\chi_p\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'})\rho'=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'})\rho_p=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}_p})\rho_p\\
&=&(\beta_G^p\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho_p)\Delta_G
=(\beta_G^p\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho')\Delta_G\\
&=&(\chi_p\otimes\pi\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes\pi)({\rm id}\otimes\rho)\Delta_G\\
&=&(\chi_p\otimes\pi\otimes\pi)({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_\mathbb{G})\rho.
\end{eqnarray*}
This shows that $\pi$ intertwines the comultiplications. It remains to show that $\pi$ is invertible. To do so, we construct the inverse of $\pi$. Consider the unital $*$-homomorphism $$\rho'_p:=(\chi_p\otimes{\rm id})\rho\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B_p\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$$
and view $C(H_p)\subset C(H)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$ and $C(F)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$. It is clear that $C(F)$ commutes with $C(H_p)$, $\rho'_p(f)=1_{B_p}\otimes f$ for $f\in C(F)$ and $[\rho_p'(a),\beta_p(b)]=0$ for all $a\in C(G)$ and $b\in B_p$. Hence there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\pi_p^{-1}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G}_p)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$ such that $({\rm id}\otimes\pi_p^{-1})\rho_p=\rho_p'$ and $\pi_p^{-1}\vert_{C(H_p)}$ is the inclusion of $C(H_p)$ in $C(\mathbb{G})$. In particular, for each vertex $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$, $\pi_p^{-1}\vert_{C(F)}$ is the inclusion of $C(F)$ in $C(\mathbb{G})$. Consider the unitaries $u_e\in C(H)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$. By the universal property of the fundamental quantum group algebra, there exists a unique morphism $\pi^{-1}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G}')\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$ such that $\pi^{-1}\vert_{C(\mathbb{G}_p)}=\pi_p^{-1}$ and $\pi^{-1}(v_e)=u_e$, for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$ and $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. It is now easy to check that $\pi^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\pi$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
When $(B,\psi)=\bigoplus(B_i,\psi)$ is the ergodic decomposition of $(B,\psi)$ and $H={\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi)$ we recover the generalization to the amalgamated case of the ergodic decomposition \cite[Proposition 5.4]{FP16} (by using example \ref{ExErgoDec}): $$G\wr_{\ast,F} {\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi)\simeq \ast_{i\in I,F}\left(G\wr_{\ast,F} {\rm Aut}^+(B_i, \psi_i)\right).$$
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{PropUnivAlphaAction}
Fix $1\leq \kappa\leq K$. For any unital C*-algebra $D_\kappa$, any unital $*$-morphism $\pi_\kappa\,:\,C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes D_\kappa$ and any {\rm faithful} unital $*$-morphism $\iota_\kappa \,:\, C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow D_\kappa$ such that, for all $a\in C(G)$, $b\in B$, $f\in C(F)$, $$\pi_\kappa(a)({\rm id}\otimes\iota_\kappa)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1_F)=({\rm id}\otimes\iota_\kappa)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1_F) \pi_\kappa(a)\text{ and }\pi_\kappa(f) = 1_\kappa\otimes \iota_\kappa(1\otimes f),$$
there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa\,:\, C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow D$ such that $$({\rm id}\otimes\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa)\rho_\kappa=\pi_\kappa\text{ and }\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa(x f)=\iota_\kappa(x\otimes f)\text{ for all }x\in C(H), f\in C(F).$$
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
If such $D_\kappa$ is given with the corresponding $*$-morphisms we define $$\mathcal{D}_0 := \underset{\gamma\neq \kappa,\, C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}{\ast} C_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$$ and $\mathcal{D}:= D_\kappa\underset{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}{\ast}\mathcal{D}_0$, where the amalgamation is with respect to the faithful unital $*$-homomorphisms $\iota_\kappa\,:\,C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow D_\kappa$ and the inclusion $C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_0$. Composing $\pi_\kappa$ (resp. $\rho_\gamma$) with the inclusion of $D_\kappa$ (resp. $C_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$ for $\gamma\neq\kappa$) in $\mathcal{D}$ we may view $\pi_\kappa\,:\,C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes \mathcal{D}$ (resp. $\rho_\gamma\,:\,C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathcal{D}$). Use the universal property of the direct sum to get a map $\rho' : C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes\mathcal{D}$ such that $(\chi_\gamma \otimes {\rm id}) \rho' = \rho_\gamma$ for $\gamma\neq \kappa$ and $(\chi_\kappa \otimes {\rm id}) \rho' = \pi_\kappa$, we also have a map $\iota\,:\,C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow \mathcal{D}$ which is the canonical inclusion. Note that, if $a\in C(G)$ and $b\in B$, the commutation relation $\rho'(a)(({\rm id}\otimes \iota)(\beta(b)\otimes 1_F)) =  (({\rm id}\otimes \iota)(\beta(b)\otimes 1_F))\rho'(a)$ can be checked when composed with any $\chi_\gamma\otimes {\rm id}$. For $f\in C(F)$, the relation $\rho'(f) = 1_B\otimes \iota(1\otimes f)$ also follows from the fact that we have the relations when applying $(\chi_\gamma\otimes {\rm id})$ and the fact that we amalgamated the different copies of $C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$.
Applying the universal property of $C(\mathbb{G})$ gives a $*$-morphism $\widetilde{\pi} : C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow \mathcal{D},$ such that $\rho' = ({\rm id}\otimes\widetilde{\pi})\circ \rho$ and $\widetilde{\pi}_{\vert C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)} =\iota$. Define $\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa :=\widetilde{\pi}_{\vert C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}\,:\, C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}) \rightarrow \mathcal{D}$. Note that $\pi_\kappa=(\chi_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})\rho'=(\chi_\kappa\otimes \widetilde{\pi})\rho=({\rm id}\otimes\widetilde{\pi})\rho_\kappa=({\rm id}\otimes \widetilde{\pi}_\kappa)\rho_\kappa$. In particular, $\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subset D_\kappa$ and we may view $\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa$ as a map from $C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ to $D_\kappa$. Hence, $\widetilde{\pi}_\kappa\vert_{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}=\iota_\kappa$ and this concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{ThmBlockAction}
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists a unique unital $*$-isomorphism
$$\pi\,:\,C_1(\mathbb{G})\underset{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}{*}\dots\underset{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}{*}C_K(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$$
such that, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, $\pi\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}\,:\, C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$ is the inclusion.
\item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, there exists a unique unital $*$-isomorphism
$$\pi_\kappa\,:\,(B\otimes C(G))\underset{B\otimes C(F)}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F))\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$$
such that $\pi_\kappa(b\otimes a)=\beta_\kappa(b)\rho_\kappa(a)$ for $b\otimes a\in B\otimes C(G)$ and $\pi_\kappa\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}$ is the inclusion. The amalgamated free product is done with respect to the inclusion map $B\otimes C(F)\rightarrow B\otimes C(G)$, and the map $\beta_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}\,:\, B\otimes C(F)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$. The inverse isomorphism $\varphi_\kappa:=\pi_\kappa^{-1}$ satisfies $\varphi_\kappa\circ\rho_\kappa(a)=1\otimes a\in B\otimes C(G)$ for all $a\in C(G)$ and $\varphi_\kappa\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}$ is the inclusion.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
$(1)$. The existence of $\pi$ follows from the universal property of the amalgamated free product. Let us construct the inverse of $\pi$. Denote by $C$ the free product of the C*-algebras $C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, amalgamated over $C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ and view $C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\subset C$. Note that we have $\rho_\kappa\,:\,C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\subset M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C$ such that $\rho_\kappa(f)=1_\kappa\otimes f$ for all $f\in C(F)$ and $1\leq\kappa\leq K$. Hence, there exists a unique $\rho'\,:\,C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C$ such that $(\chi_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})\rho'=\rho_\kappa$ for all $\kappa$ and $\rho'(f) = 1_B\otimes f$ for all $f\in C(F)$. Since the images of $\rho_\kappa$ and $\beta_\kappa$ commute in $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ for all $\kappa$, it follows that the images of $\rho'$ and $\beta$ commute in $B\otimes C$. By the universal property of $C(\mathbb{G})$, there exists a unique $\varphi\,:\,C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C$ such that $\varphi\vert_{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}$ is the inclusion and $({\rm id}\otimes\varphi)\rho=\rho'$. It is clear that $\varphi$ is the inverse of $\pi$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. During this proof we use the notation: $$\mathcal{A}_\kappa:=(B\otimes C(G))\underset{B\otimes C(F)}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F))$$
and we write $\nu_\kappa\,:\, B\otimes C(G)\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ and $\mu_\kappa\,:\, M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_\kappa$ the canonical faithful unital $*$-homomorphisms. They satisfy $\mu_\kappa(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes f)=\nu_\kappa(b\otimes f)$ for all $b\in B$ and $f\in C(F)$. We fix once and for all a basis of $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ consisting of matrix units $(e^\kappa_{ij})_{ij}$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent The existence of $\pi_\kappa$ is a consequence of the universal property of the amalgamated free product $\mathcal{A}_\kappa$. Let us construct its inverse $\varphi_\kappa\,:\,M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$. We define the morphism $\iota\,:\,C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_\kappa$, $x\otimes f\mapsto\mu_\kappa(1\otimes x\otimes f)$ and we consider the elements
$$\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(a):=\sum_{s=1}^{N_\kappa}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\in\mathcal{A}_\kappa\text{ for }a\in C(G)\text{ and }1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa.$$ A direct computation gives the relations:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(ab)=\sum_k\varphi^\kappa_{ik}(a)\varphi^\kappa_{kj}(b)$.
    \item $(\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(a))^*=\varphi^\kappa_{ji}(a^*)$.
    \item $\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(1)=\delta_{ij}1_{\mathcal{A}_\kappa}$.
    \item $\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(f)= \delta_{ij}\iota(1\otimes f)$ if $f\in C(F)$.
\end{enumerate}
Note that $(ii)$, $(iii)$ and $(iv)$ are clear so we only prove $(i)$. Let $a,b\in C(G)$ then,
\begin{eqnarray*}
    \sum_{k=1}^{N_\kappa} \varphi^{\kappa}_{ik}(a)\varphi^{\kappa}_{kj}(b)&=&\sum_{k,s}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{kk}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes b)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
    &=&\sum_{s}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes ab)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)=\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(ab).
\end{eqnarray*}

\noindent This relations mean that $\varphi_\kappa\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ defined by $\varphi_\kappa(a):=\sum_{i,j=1}^{N_\kappa}e^\kappa_{ij}\otimes\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(a)$ is a unital $*$-homomorphism. Let us check that $\varphi_\kappa(a)$ and $({\rm id}\otimes\iota)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1)$ commutes, for all $a\in C(G)$ and $b\in B$. We write $\beta_\kappa\,:\,B\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)$ with coefficients $\beta_\kappa(b)=\sum_{i,j}e^\kappa_{ij}\otimes\beta^\kappa_{ij}(b)$. Then, for all $b\in B$,
$$(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1)\beta_\kappa(b)=\sum_re^\kappa_{sr}\otimes\beta^\kappa_{ir}(b)\quad\text{and}\quad\beta_\kappa(b)(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1)=\sum_re^\kappa_{rs}\otimes\beta^\kappa_{rj}(b).$$
Hence, writing $({\rm id}\otimes\iota)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1)\varphi_\kappa(a)=\sum_{i,j}e^\kappa_{ij}\otimes X^\kappa_{ij}$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
X^\kappa_{ij}&=&\sum_{r,s}\iota(\beta^\kappa_{ir}(b)\otimes 1)\varphi^\kappa_{rj}(a)=\sum_{r,s}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{sr}\otimes\beta^\kappa_{ir}(b)\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\sum_s\mu_\kappa((e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1)\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\sum_s\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(b\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\sum_s\mu_\kappa((e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(\beta_\kappa(b)(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1)\otimes 1)\\
&=&\sum_{r,s}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{rs}\otimes\beta^\kappa_{rj}(b)\otimes 1)=\sum_r\varphi^\kappa_{ir}(a)\iota(\beta^\kappa_{rj}(b)\otimes 1).
\end{eqnarray*}

\noindent This shows that $({\rm id}\otimes\iota)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1)\varphi_\kappa(a)=\varphi_\kappa(a)({\rm id}\otimes\iota)(\beta_\kappa(b)\otimes 1)$ for all $a\in C(G)$ and $b\in B$. Note that, for all $f\in C(F)$, $\varphi_\kappa(f) = \sum_{i,j} e_{ij}^\kappa \otimes \delta_{ij}\iota(1\otimes f) = 1_\kappa \otimes \iota(1\otimes f)$. The universal property of $C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ (Proposition \ref{PropUnivAlphaAction}) gives a unital $*$-homomorphism, still denoted $\varphi_\kappa\,:\,C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ such that $\varphi_\kappa(\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))=\varphi^\kappa_{ij}(a)$ for all $1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa$ and all $a\in C(G)$ and $\varphi_\kappa(x\otimes f)=\mu_\kappa(1\otimes x\otimes f)$ for all $x\in C(H)$ and $f\in C(F)$. Now, we note that $\varphi_\kappa(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subseteq\mu_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes 1\otimes 1)'\cap\mathcal{A}_\kappa$. Indeed, it is clear that, for all $x\in C(H)$ and $f\in C(F)$, $\varphi_\kappa(x\otimes f)=\mu_\kappa(1\otimes x\otimes f)$ commutes with $\mu_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes 1\otimes 1)$ and, if $x=\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)$ is a coefficient of $\rho_\kappa$, then:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\varphi_\kappa(x)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{rs}\otimes 1\otimes 1)&=&\sum_t\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{ti}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{jt}e^\kappa_{rs}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\ &=&\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{ri}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{rs}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\varphi_\kappa(x).
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, $\varphi_\kappa(x)$ commutes with $\mu_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes 1\otimes 1)$ for any $x$ which is a coefficients of $\rho_\kappa$. Since $C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ is generated by $C(H)$ and coefficients of $\rho_\kappa$, it follows that
$$\varphi_\kappa(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subseteq\mu_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes 1\otimes 1)'\cap\mathcal{A}_\kappa.$$
Hence, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism, still denoted $\varphi_\kappa\,:\, M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ such that $\varphi_\kappa(b\otimes x)=\mu_\kappa(b\otimes 1\otimes 1)\varphi_\kappa(x)$, for all $b\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ and $x\in C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$. By construction we have $\varphi_\kappa\circ\rho_\kappa(a)=\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)$ for all $a\in C(G)$ and $\varphi_\kappa\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}=\mu_\kappa$. Since $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ is generated, as a C*-algebra, by $\rho_\kappa(C(G))\cup M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ this easily implies that $\varphi_\kappa$ is the inverse of $\pi_\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{LemReducedAction}
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $X_\kappa:=\mathcal{C}_\kappa +M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)$ is a dense subalgebra of $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$.
    \item There exists a unique conditional expectation $$\mathbb{E}_\kappa\,:\,M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\text{ such that }\ker(\mathbb{E}_\kappa)=\overline{\mathcal{C}_\kappa}.$$
    \item $\Delta(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subset C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and $({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes\Delta)(\mathcal{C}_\kappa)\subset\mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes  C(\mathbb{G})$.
    \item For all $X\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ one has:
    $$( \mathbb{E}_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_{C(\mathbb{G})})({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes\Delta)(X)=({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes \Delta)\mathbb{E}_\kappa(X).$$
    \item For all $X\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ one has:
    $$(({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)\circ\mathbb{E}_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_{C(\mathbb{G})})({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes\Delta)(X)=({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)\circ\mathbb{E}_\kappa(X)\otimes 1_{C(\mathbb{G})}.$$
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
$(1)$. It is easy to see that $X_\kappa$ is a unital $*$-subalgebra of $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ containing $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)$. Note that it also contains $1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)$ for all $a\in {\rm Pol}(G)$. Indeed, writing $1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)=\sum_r(e^\kappa_{ri}\otimes 1)\rho_\kappa(a)(e^\kappa_{jr}\otimes 1)$ and $e^{\kappa}_{rs}=(e^\kappa_{rs})^\circ+\frac{\delta_{rs}}{\delta\lambda_{\kappa,r}}1_B$, where $E_\kappa((e^\kappa_{rs})^\circ\otimes 1)=0$ we see that $1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)\in X$ when $E_F(a)=0$ and, for any $a\in {\rm Pol}(G)$, writing $a=a^\circ+E_F(a)$ we have $\rho_{ij}^\kappa(a)=\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a^\circ)+\rho^\kappa_{ij}(E_F(a)) = \rho^\kappa_{ij}(a^\circ) + \delta_{ij}(1\otimes 1\otimes E_F(a))$ which implies that $1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)\in X$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. \noindent As in the proof of Theorem \ref{ThmBlockAction}, we write 
$$\mathcal{A}_\kappa:=(B\otimes C(G))\underset{B\otimes C(F)}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)),$$
where the amalgamation is with respect to the inclusion $B\otimes C(F)\rightarrow B\otimes C(G)$ and the unital $*$-homomorphism $\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_F\,:\, B\otimes C(F)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ and we write $\nu_\kappa\,:\, B\otimes C(G)\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ and $\mu_\kappa\,:\, M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_\kappa$ the canonical faithful unital $*$-homomorphism. Consider the unique ucp map $E_2\,:\,\mathcal{A}_\kappa\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ such that $E_2\circ\mu_\kappa={\rm id}$, $E_2\circ\nu_\kappa=\beta_\kappa\otimes E_F$ and $E_2(x)=0$ for all $x$ reduced of length $\geq 2$ in $\mathcal{A}_\kappa$ in the amalgamated free product sense and with respect to the ucp maps $({\rm id}\otimes E_F)\,:\,B\otimes C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C(F)$ and
$$E_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}_F\,:\, M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\rightarrow B\otimes C(F).$$
Recall that $\varphi_\kappa:=\pi_\kappa^{-1}\,:\, M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_\kappa$ is constructed in Theorem \ref{ThmBlockAction}. Define the ucp map $\mathbb{E}_\kappa:=E_2\circ\varphi_\kappa\,:\,M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$. 

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent If $x=X_0\rho_\kappa(a_1)X_1\dots \rho_\kappa(a_n)X_n$ ($n\geq 1$) is reduced then $$\varphi_\kappa(x)=\mu_\kappa(X_0)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a_1)\dots\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a_n)\mu_\kappa(X_n)$$
is reduced in $\mathcal{A}_\kappa$ of length at least $2$ so $E_2(y)=0$. It follows that $\mathbb{E}_\kappa(x)=E_2(y)=0$. We prove in the same way that $\mathbb{E}_\kappa(x)=0$ for all types of reduced operators. Hence, $\mathbb{E}_\kappa(\mathcal{C}_\kappa)=\{0\}$. Recall that $\varphi_\kappa\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes C(F)}=\mu_\kappa$ and $E_2\circ\mu_\kappa={\rm id}$. Hence, $\mathbb{E}_\kappa\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}={\rm id}$. It remains to show that $\ker(\mathbb{E}_\kappa)\subset \overline{\mathcal{C}_\kappa}$ and this follows from $(1)$ and the fact that $\mathbb{E}_\kappa$ is the identity on the subalgebra $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(3)$ By definition $\Delta$ we have, writing $\Delta_G(a)=\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}$, with $a_{(1)},a_{(2)}\in{\rm Pol}(G)$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(\rho_\kappa(a))&=&\sum(\chi_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})(a_{(1)}\otimes \rho(a_{(2)}))\\
&=&\sum_{\gamma,k,l}(\chi_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G(a_{(1)}\otimes e^\gamma_{kl})\otimes\rho^\gamma_{kl}(a_{(2)})\\
&=&\sum_{\gamma,k,l}\left[\rho_\kappa(a_{(1)})(\beta_\kappa(e^\gamma_{kl})\otimes 1_{C(F)})\right]\otimes\rho^\gamma_{kl}(a_{(2)})
\end{eqnarray*}
Since $\Delta(C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F))=\Delta_{H\times F}(C(H\times F))\subset (C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)) \otimes (C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F))$ we conclude easily that $\Delta(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subset C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Let $x$ be a reduced operator and let us show that $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$. We prove our statement for $x$ a reduced operator of the form $x=\rho_\kappa(a_1)X_1\dots \rho_\kappa(a_n)X_n$, the proof for other types of reduced operator is the same.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textbf{Claim.} \textit{If for all $s$, $X_s\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H)\otimes\mathbb{C}1_{C(F)}$ then $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$.}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{Proof of the Claim.} Write $x=\rho_\kappa(a_1)(X_1\otimes 1)\dots \rho_\kappa(a_n)(X_n\otimes 1)$, where $X_s\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H)$ is such that $E_\kappa(X_s)=0$. Writing $X_s\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)$ as $X_s=\sum_{i_s,j_s}b^\kappa_{i_sj_s}\otimes x_{i_sj_s}$ and $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(X_s\otimes 1)=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_H)(X_s)\otimes 1_{C(F)}=\sum (X_s)_{(1)}\otimes (X_s)_{(2)}$ where $$(X_s)_{(1)}=b^\kappa_{i_sj_s}\otimes (x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)}\otimes 1\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H)\otimes{\rm Pol}(F)\text{ and},$$
$$(X_s)_{(2)}=(x_{i_sj_s})_{(2)}\otimes 1\in {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes{\rm Pol}(F)$$ with $\Delta_{H}(x_{i_sj_s})=\sum(x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)}\otimes (x_{i_sj_s})_{(2)}$, we obtain:
$$
({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)=\sum\rho_\kappa((a_1)_{(1)})(\beta_\kappa(e^{\gamma_1}_{k_1l_1})\otimes 1)(X_1)_{(1)}\dots\rho_\kappa((a_n)_{(1)})(\beta_\kappa(e^{\gamma_n}_{k_nl_n})\otimes 1)(X_n)_{(1)}$$
$$\otimes\rho^{\gamma_1}_{k_1l_1}((a_1)_{(2)})(X_1)_{(2)}\dots \rho^{\gamma_n}_{k_nl_n}((a_n)_{(2)})(X_n)_{(2)}.$$
Where $\Delta_G(a_k)=\sum (a_k)_{(1)}\otimes (a_k)_{(2)}$ and $E_F((a_k)_{(1)})=0$. If  $(E_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}_F)((X_s)_{(1)})=0$, for all $s$, then $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\in \mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$, since $$(E_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}_F)((\beta_\kappa(e^{\gamma_s}_{k_sl_s})\otimes 1)(X_s)_{(1)})=e^{\gamma_s}_{k_sl_s}(E_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}_F)((X_s)_{(1)})=0.$$ Otherwise, we write $(X_s)_{(1)}=(X_s)_{(1)}^\circ+(\beta_\kappa E_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_F)((X_s)_{(1)})$, where $(E_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_F)((X_s)_{(1)}^\circ)=0$ so that we may decompose $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)$ as the sum of two terms $Y_s+Z_s$ where in $Y_s$ is the same as $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)$ but replacing $(X_s)_{(1)}$ by $(X_s)_{(1)}^\circ$ and the second term is:
$$Z_s=\sum\rho_\kappa((a_1)_{(1)})\dots(\beta_\kappa(e^{\gamma_s}_{k_sl_s})\otimes 1)(\beta_\kappa E_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_F)(b^\kappa_{i_sj_s}\otimes (x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)}\otimes 1)\dots (X_n)_{(1)}$$
$$\otimes\rho^{\gamma_1}_{k_1l_1}((a_1)_{(2)})(X_1)_{(2)}\dots \rho^{\gamma_n}_{k_nl_n}((a_n)_{(2)})(X_n)_{(2)}.$$
By Proposition \ref{PropUcpSection} we have:
$$E_\kappa(b^\kappa_{i_sj_s}\otimes (x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)})=\delta^{-1}\lambda_{\kappa,i_s}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\lambda_{\kappa,j_s}^{-\frac{3}{2}}\sum_{\beta,r,t}\left(\frac{\lambda_{\beta,r}}{\lambda_{\beta,t}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}h_H(u^{j_si_s,\kappa}_{tr,\beta}(x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)})b^\beta_{rt}$$
Replacing this expression in $Z_s$ we get:
$$Z_s=\delta^{-1}\sum\left(\frac{\lambda_{\beta,r}}{\lambda_{\beta,t}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\rho_\kappa((a_1)_{(1)})\dots(\beta_\kappa(e^{\gamma_s}_{k_sl_s}b^\beta_{rt})\otimes 1)\rho_\kappa((a_{s+1})_{(1)})\dots $$
$$\otimes(\rho)^{\gamma_1}_{k_1l_1}((a_1)_{(2)})\dots\left(\sum_{i_s,j_s,(1)',(2)'}\lambda_{\kappa,i_s}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\lambda_{\kappa,j_s}^{-\frac{3}{2}}h_H(u^{j_si_s,\kappa}_{tr,\beta}(x_{i_sj_s})_{(1)'})(x_{i_sj_s})_{(2)'}\right)\dots$$
Since $E_\kappa(X_s)=0$, we may now use Lemma \ref{LemE} to deduce that $Z_s=0$. Doing that for all $s$, we conclude that $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$.$\hfill$ $\qed$

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{End of the proof of $(3)$.} Fix a basis $(y_k)_k$ of ${\rm Pol}(F)$. If now $x$ is an arbitrary reduced operator of the form $x=\rho_\kappa(a_1)X_1\dots \rho_\kappa(a_n)X_n$, with $X_s\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes{\rm Pol}(F)$, we may write $X_s$ as a finite sum $X_s=\sum_kX_{s,k}\otimes y_k$, where $X_{s,k}\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H)$. Since $x$ is reduced one has $\sum_k E_\kappa(X_{s,k})y_k=(E_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(X_s)=0$. Since the family $(y_k)_k$ is linearly independent we obtain $E_\kappa(X_{s,k})=0$ for all $k$. Write $x$ as a finite sum:
\begin{eqnarray*}
x&=&\sum_{k_1,\dots k_n}\rho_\kappa(a_1)(X_{1,k_1}\otimes y_{k_1})\dots \rho_\kappa(a_n)(X_{n,k_n}\otimes y_{k_n})\\
&=&\sum_{k_1,\dots k_n}\rho_\kappa(a_1y_{k_1})(X_{1,k_1}\otimes 1)\dots \rho_\kappa(a_ny_{k_n})(X_{n,k_n}\otimes 1),
\end{eqnarray*}
where, in the last equality, we used the relations $\rho_\kappa(f)=1\otimes1\otimes f$, for all $f\in C(F)$. Since $E_F(a_sy_{k_s})=E_F(a_s)y_{k_s}=0$ for all $s$, we deduce from the Claim that $x\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(4)$. By $(1)$, it suffices to prove the formula for $X\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa$ and for $X\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)$. If $X\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa$ we have $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(X)\in\mathcal{C}_\kappa\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ by $(3)$. It now follows from $(2)$ that
$$(\mathbb{E}_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_{C(\mathbb{G})})({\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}}\otimes\Delta)(X)=0=\mathbb{E}_\kappa(X)\otimes 1_{C(\mathbb{G})}.$$
If now $X\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)$ then, since $\Delta\vert_{C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)}=\Delta_{H\times F}$,
$$({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(X)\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F),$$
and therefore $(\mathbb{E}_\kappa\otimes{\rm id}_{C(\mathbb{G})})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(X) = ({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(X) =({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)\mathbb{E}_\kappa$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(5)$. It suffices to apply $({\rm id}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F\otimes{\rm id})$ to the equation proved in $(4)$ and use the fact that the Haar state of $H\times F$ is $h_H\otimes h_F$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{RemarkErgodic}
We have $(\iota\otimes{\rm id})\circ\Delta=\widetilde{\Delta}\circ\iota$ and $(\widetilde{\Delta}\otimes{\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)\widetilde{\Delta}$. Indeed, $x\in C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, we have $\widetilde{\Delta}\circ\iota(x) = \widetilde{\Delta}(1\otimes x) =({\rm id} \otimes \Delta)(1\otimes x) = (\iota\otimes {\rm id})\Delta(x)$ and, since $\Delta(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subset C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and $\Delta$ is co-associative, one has, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
    (\widetilde{\Delta} \otimes {\rm id}) \widetilde{\Delta}\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})} &=& (\widetilde{\Delta} \otimes {\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes \Delta\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}) = ({\rm id}\otimes \Delta\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}\otimes {\rm id})({\rm id} \otimes \Delta\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})\\&=& ({\rm id}\otimes {\rm id}\otimes \Delta\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})({\rm id} \otimes \Delta\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})= ({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)\widetilde{\Delta}\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}.
\end{eqnarray*}
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{TheoremErgodic}One has $(E\otimes {\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}= \Delta_{H\times F} \circ E$. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $((E\circ \iota)\otimes{\rm id})\Delta=\Delta_{H\times F}\circ (E\circ  \iota)$ so $h_\mathbb{G}:= (h_H\otimes h_F)\circ (E\circ\iota)$ and $E\circ\iota=E_{H\times F}$ is the conditional expectation $C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(H\times F)$ of the dual quantum subgroup $H\times F$.
    \item $({\rm id}_B \otimes E\circ\iota)\rho = 1_B\otimes 1_{C(H)} \otimes E_F(\cdot)$ therefore $({\rm id}_B\otimes h_\mathbb{G})\rho=h_G(\cdot) 1_B$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
We start with the following Claim.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textbf{Claim.} \textit{$\ker(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa)=\overline{\mathcal{C}_\kappa+\ker(\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)}$.}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{Proof of the Claim.} Let $x\in\ker(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa)$. By Lemma \ref{LemReducedAction} $(1)$, there are sequences $(x_n)$ and $(y_n)$ such that $x_n\in \mathcal{C}_\kappa$ and $y_n\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes {\rm Pol}(F)$ such that $x_n+y_n\rightarrow x$. Hence, $$\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa(x_n)+\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa(y_n)=(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(y_n)\rightarrow \widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa(x)=0.$$
Define $y_n^\circ:=y_n-1_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})}\otimes(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(y_n)$ so that $(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(y_n^\circ)=0$. Note that  $y_n^\circ\in\ker(\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H)\otimes{\rm Pol}(F)$ and $x_n+y_n^\circ\rightarrow x$.$\hfill$ $\qed$

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{End of the proof of Theorem.} Suppose that $x\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ then, since $\widetilde{\Delta}(x)=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ one has, by Lemma \ref{LemReducedAction},
\begin{eqnarray*}
(E\otimes {\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}(x)&=&(E\otimes {\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)=(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_\kappa\otimes {\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\\
&=&(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\mathbb{E}_\kappa\otimes {\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x)\\
&=&(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes\Delta)\mathbb{E}_\kappa(x)=\Delta\circ E(x)=\Delta_{H\times F}\circ E(x).
\end{eqnarray*}
In particular, $(E\otimes {\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}(x)=\Delta_{H\times F}\circ E(x)$ for $x\in C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)\subset C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and it remains to show that the formula holds for any reduced operator $x$ in $C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Write such a reduced operator $x=x_1\dots x_n\in C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$, $x_s\in M_{N_{\kappa_s}}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\kappa_s}(\mathbb{G})$ with $\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_{\kappa_s}(x_s)=0$ and $\kappa_s\neq\kappa_{s+1}$ so that $E(x)=0$. It suffices to show that $(E\otimes {\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}(x)=0$. By linearity, continuity and the Claim, we may and will assume that, for all $s$, $x_s\in\mathcal{C}_{\kappa_s}\cup\ker(\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes {\rm Pol}(H)\otimes{\rm Pol}(F)$. Since
$$\widetilde{\Delta}(x)=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x_1)\dots({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(x_s),$$
$\widetilde{\Delta}(x)$ is an alternating product from $({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(\mathcal{C}_{\kappa_s})\subset\mathcal{C}_{\kappa_s}\otimes C(\mathbb{G})\subset \ker(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_{\kappa_s})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ (Lemma \ref{LemReducedAction}) and we deduce from:
$$({\rm id}\otimes\Delta)(\ker(\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H\times F))\subset \ker(\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H\times F)\otimes C(\mathbb{G})\subset\ker(\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}_{\kappa_s})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$$
that $(E\otimes{\rm id})\widetilde{\Delta}(x)=0$. It proves the first statement of the Theorem.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(1)$. We use Remark \ref{RemarkErgodic} and the previous statement to deduce the first equation. Then, applying $h_H\otimes h_F\otimes{\rm id}$ shows that $(h_H\otimes h_F)\circ E\circ\iota$ is $\Delta$-invariant hence, $h_\mathbb{G}=(h_H\otimes h_F)\circ E\circ\iota$. We conclude the proof of $(1)$ by Remark \ref{RmkEF} $(3)$.


\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. Let $a\in C(G)$ and write $\rho(a)=\sum_{\kappa,i,j} e^\kappa_{ij}\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)$. We use the notations of Theorem \ref{ThmBlockAction}, Lemma \ref{LemReducedAction} and their proofs. By construction of $E$ we have: \begin{eqnarray*}
E\circ\iota(\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))&=&E(1\otimes \rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))=(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})\mathbb{E}_\kappa(1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))\\
&=&(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})E_2\circ\varphi_\kappa(1\otimes\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))\\
&=&\sum_{s=1}^{N_\kappa}(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})E_2\left(\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\right)\\
&=&\sum_{s=1}^{N_\kappa}(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})((e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)(\beta_\kappa\otimes E_F) (1\otimes a)(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1))\\
&=&\delta_{ij}1_{C(H)}\otimes E_F(a).
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, $({\rm id}_B\otimes E\circ\iota)\rho(a)=\sum_{\kappa,i}e^\kappa_{ii}\otimes 1_{C(H)}\otimes E_F(a)=1_B\otimes 1_{C(H)}\otimes E_F(a)$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{PropDualSUbGroups}
The map $\iota_\Lambda$ is faithful and intertwines the comultiplications so that $\mathbb{G}_\Lambda$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Consider the two canonical maps $\beta_G\,:\, C(G)\otimes B\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and $\beta_\Lambda\,:\, C(\Lambda)\otimes B\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}_\Lambda)$ and note that, by definition, $({\rm id}\otimes\iota_\Lambda)\beta_\Lambda=\beta_G\vert_{C(\Lambda)\otimes B}$. It follows easily that $$({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_\mathbb{G}\circ\iota_\Lambda)\rho_\Lambda=({\rm id}\otimes(\iota_\Lambda\otimes\iota_\Lambda)\circ\Delta_{\mathbb{G}_\Lambda})\rho_\Lambda$$ which implies that $\iota_\Lambda$ intertwines the comultiplications. Let us now show that $\iota_\Lambda$ is faithful. By Proposition \ref{dualqsg}, it suffices to show that $\iota_\Lambda$ intertwines the Haar states (since it will imply that it is faithful at the reduced level). Note that, for $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, $\iota_\Lambda(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}_\Lambda))\subset C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$. Hence, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\widetilde{\iota}_\Lambda\,:\, C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\Lambda)\rightarrow C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ such that:
$$\widetilde{\iota}_\Lambda\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}_\Lambda)}={\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})}\otimes\iota_\Lambda\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})},\text{ for all }1\leq\kappa\leq K.$$
By construction, $\widetilde{\iota}_\Lambda$ maps reduced operators in $C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\Lambda)$ to reduced operators in $C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and is the identity on $C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$. By uniqueness property, we have $E\circ\iota_\Lambda=E_\Lambda$, where $E\,:\, C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\rightarrow C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ and $E_\Lambda\,:\, C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\Lambda)\rightarrow C(H)\otimes_{{\rm max}} C(F)$ are the canonical ucp maps constructed in Section \ref{SectionBlockExtended}. It follows from Theorem \ref{TheoremErgodic} that $\iota_\Lambda$ intertwines the Haar states.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
There is a canonical isomorphism $G\wr_{*,\beta,\widehat{\Gamma}} H\simeq\pi_1(\mathbb{G}_p,\mathbb{G}_e,\mathcal{G},\mathcal{T})$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Write $\mathbb{G}:=G\wr_{*,\beta,\widehat{\Gamma}} H$ with canonical morphism $\rho\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and view $C(H),C^*(\Gamma)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$. We also write $\mathbb{G}':=\pi_1(\mathbb{G}_p,\mathbb{G}_e,\mathcal{G},\mathcal{T})$, we view $C(H)\subset C(\mathbb{G}_p)\subset C(\mathbb{G}')$ and we denote $$C(\mathbb{G}')=\langle C(\mathbb{G}_p),v_e\,\vert\,p\in V(\mathcal{G}),e\in E(\mathcal{G})\rangle\text{ and }C(G)=\langle C(G_p),u_e\,\vert\,p\in V(\mathcal{G}),e\in E(\mathcal{G})\rangle.$$
View, for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$, $\rho_p\,:\,C(G_p)\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}_p)\subset B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')$ and note that, for all $b\in C(\Lambda_e)$, $$\rho_{s(e)}(s_e(b))=({\rm id}\otimes s_e')\rho_e(b)=(1_B\otimes v_{e}^*)({\rm id}\otimes r_e')(\rho_e(b))(1_B\otimes v_e)=(1_B\otimes v_{e}^*)\rho_{r(e)}\circ r_e(b)(1_B\otimes v_e).$$
The universal property of $C(G)$ gives a unique unital $*$-homomorphism
$$\rho'\,:\, C(G)\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')\text{ such that }\rho'\vert_{C(G_p)}=\rho_p,\,\,\rho'(u_e)=1_B\otimes v_e\text{ for all }p\in V(\mathcal{G}),e\in E(\mathcal{G}).$$ By construction of $\rho'$, one has $\rho'(C^*(\Gamma))\subset \mathbb{C} 1_B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')$ hence, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\widehat{\Gamma}}\,:\,C^*(\Gamma)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')$ such that $\rho'(f)=1_B\otimes\iota_{\widehat{\Gamma}}(f)$ for all $f\in C^*(\Gamma)$. Note that for all $p\in V(\mathcal{G})$, $a\in C(G_p)$ and $b\in B$, $\rho'(a)\beta(b)=\rho_p(a)\beta(b)=\beta(b)\rho_p(a)=\beta(b)\rho'(a)$. Moreover, since each $s_e'$ is the identity on $C(H)$, each $v_e$ commutes with $C(H)$ inside $C(\mathbb{G}')$ hence, $\rho'(u_e)\beta(b)=(1_B\otimes v_e)\beta(b)=\beta(b)(1_B\otimes v_e)$ for all $b\in B$ and $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. Also, $C(H)$ commutes with $\iota_{\widehat{\Gamma}}(C^*(\Gamma))$. By the universal property of the free wreath product C*-algebra $C(\mathbb{G})$, there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\pi\,:\, C(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}')$ such that $({\rm id}\otimes\pi)\rho=\rho'$, $\pi\vert_{C(H)}$ is the inclusion and $\pi\vert_{C^*(\Gamma)}=\iota_{\widehat{\Gamma}}$. Writing $\beta_G\,:\, C(G)\otimes B\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ and $\beta_{G_p}\,:\, C(G_p)\otimes B\rightarrow B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}_p)\subset B\otimes C(\mathbb{G}')$ the canonical morphisms we have, by construction, $\beta_{G_p}=({\rm id}\otimes\pi)\circ\beta_G\vert_{C(G_p)\otimes B}$. For $a\in C(G_p)\subset C(G)$ one has:
\begin{eqnarray*}
({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}\pi)\rho(a)&=&({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'})\rho'(a)=({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}_p})\rho_p(a)=(\beta_{G_p}\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho_p)\Delta_{G_p}(a)\\
&=&({\rm id}\otimes\pi\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho')\Delta_{G_p}(a)\\
&=&({\rm id}\otimes\pi\otimes\pi)(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho)\Delta_G(a)
=({\rm id}\otimes(\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta_\mathbb{G})\rho.
\end{eqnarray*}
Since $\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}\pi(u_e)=\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}(v_e)=v_e\otimes v_e=(\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}(u_e)$ and,
$$\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}\circ\pi\vert_{C(H)}=\Delta_{\mathbb{G}'}\vert_{C(H)}=\Delta_H=(\pi\otimes\pi)\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}\vert_{C(H)}$$
we deduce that $\pi$ intertwines the comultiplications.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent We now show that $\pi$ is an isomorphism by constructing its inverse morphism $\pi^{-1}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G}')\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$. We first note that, by the universal property of the free wreath product C*-algebra $C(\mathbb{G}_p)$, there exists a unique $\pi_p^{-1}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G}_p)\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$ such that $({\rm id}\otimes\pi_p^{-1})\rho_p=\rho\vert_{C(\mathbb{G}_p)}$ and $\pi^{-1}_p\vert_{C(H)}$ is the inclusion. Viewing $C^*(\Gamma)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$, we have the relation $\rho(u_e)=1_B\otimes u_e$, for all $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$. Note that, for all $e\in E(\mathcal{G})$ and $b\in C(\Lambda_e)$ one has,
\begin{eqnarray*}
({\rm id}\otimes\pi^{-1}_{s(e)}\circ s_e')\rho_e(b)&=&({\rm id}\otimes\pi^{-1}_{s(e)})\rho_{s(e)}\circ s_e(b)=\rho\circ s_e(b)=\rho(u_e)^*\rho(r_e(b))\rho(u_e)\\
&=&\rho(u_e)^*({\rm id}\otimes\pi^{-1}_{r(e)})\rho_{r(e)}\circ r_e(b)\rho(u_e)\\
&=&\rho(u_e)^*({\rm id}\otimes\pi^{-1}_{r(e)}\circ r_e')\rho_e(b)\rho(u_e)\\
&=&(1\otimes u_e^*)({\rm id}\otimes\pi^{-1}_{r(e)}\circ r_e')\rho_e(b)(1\otimes u_e).
\end{eqnarray*}
Moreover, $\pi_{s(e)}^{-1}\circ s_e'\vert_{C(H)}$ is the inclusion of $C(H)\subset C(\mathbb{G})$ and since $C(H)$ commutes with $C^*(\Gamma)$ in  $C(\mathbb{G})$, the universal property of $C(\mathbb{G}')$ gives a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\pi^{-1}\,:\, C(\mathbb{G}')\rightarrow C(\mathbb{G})$ such that $\pi^{-1}\vert_{C(\mathbb{G}_p)}=\pi_p^{-1}$ and $\pi^{-1}(v_e)=u_e$. It is easy to check that $\pi^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\pi$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{ThmReduced}
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item One has $C_r(\mathbb{G})=\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota(C(\mathbb{G}))$ with GNS map $\lambda_\mathbb{G}=\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota$. Moreover, $E_r\vert_{C_r(\mathbb{G})}=E^r_{H\times F}$ is the reduced conditional expectation associated to the dual quantum subgroup $H\times F$.
\item One has $C_r(\mathbb{G})=\underset{C_r(H\times F)}{*}\left(C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}),E_r\vert_{C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})}\right)$.
\item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, there is a unique unital $*$-isomorphism:
$$\pi_{r,\kappa}\,:\,C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$$
such that $\pi_{r,\kappa}\circ\widetilde{\lambda}_\kappa=({\rm id}\otimes(\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota)\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})\pi_\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
$(1)$. By construction, $\lambda_{H\times F}\circ E=E_r\circ\widetilde{\lambda}$. Since $E_r$ is faithful and $\widetilde{\lambda}$ is surjective, we deduce that $C_r(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is the reduced C*-algebra of $\lambda_{H\times F}\circ E$ and it follows from Remark \ref{RmkReducedUcp} that $\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota(C(\mathbb{G}))$ is the reduced C*-algebra of $\lambda_{H\times F}\circ E\circ\iota=\lambda_{H\times F}\circ E_{H\times F}$. We conclude the proof of $(1)$ using Remark \ref{RmkEF} $(1)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. Since $C(\mathbb{G})$ is generated by the algebras $C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, for $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, we conclude that $C_r(\mathbb{G})=\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota(C(\mathbb{G}))$ is generated by $C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})=\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$  ($1\leq\kappa\leq K$). Moreover, since the $C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ are free with amalgamation with respect to $E_r\vert_{C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}=(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})\circ E_{2,\kappa}$ and since $C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\subset C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ the result follows.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(3)$. We construct the inverse isomorphism $\varphi_{r,\kappa}\,:\, M_{N_\kappa(\mathbb{C})}\otimes C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ satisfying $\varphi_{r,\kappa}\circ({\rm id}\otimes(\widetilde{\lambda}\circ\iota)\vert_{C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})=\widetilde{\lambda}_\kappa\circ\varphi_\kappa$. We view both $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\subset C_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\subset C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ in the obvious way. Note that, since $\varphi_\kappa\circ\iota(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})'\cap C_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ we deduce that $C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\subseteq M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})'\cap C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Hence, there exists a unique faithful unital $*$-homomorphism $\varphi_{r,\kappa}\,:\,M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\rightarrow C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$, such that $\varphi_{r,\kappa}(b\otimes x)=bx$ for all $b\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ and $x\in C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}).$
Since $C_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is generated by $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\varphi_\kappa\circ\iota(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$ and since $\widetilde{\lambda}_\kappa$ is surjective we deduce that $C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is generated by $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\widetilde{\lambda}_\kappa(\varphi_\kappa\circ\iota (C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})))=C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$. Both these C*-subalgebras are in the image of $\varphi_{r,\kappa}$ so $\varphi_{r,\kappa}$ is surjective.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{CorExact}
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ are exact.
    \item $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ is exact.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
$(1)\Rightarrow(2)$. Suppose that $C_r(G)$ and $C_r(H)$ are exact then, since $C_r(F)\subset C_r(G)$ is a C*-subalgebra, $C_r(F)$ is also exact. Theorem \ref{ThmReduced} and \cite[Theorem 3.2]{Dy04} implies that $C_r(\mathbb{G})$ is exact.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)\Rightarrow(1)$. Assume that $C_r(\mathbb{G})$ is exact and fix $1\leq \kappa\leq K$. Since $C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\subset C_r(\mathbb{G})$ is a C*-subalgebra, we deduce that $C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$ is exact so $C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\simeq M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{r,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$ is also exact. Finally, since both $C_r(G), C_r(H)\subset C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ are C*-subalgebras, it concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=\underset{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F)}{\ast} (L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}),E''\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and $E''_{H\times F}:=\widetilde{E}''\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}$ is the conditional expectation of the dual quantum subgroup $H\times F$.
    \item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, there is a unique unital normal $*$-isomorphism:
$$\pi''_{\kappa}\,:\,L_{\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_{\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$$
such that $\pi''_{\kappa}\vert_{C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}=\pi_{r,\kappa}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
$(1).$ Let $M:=\underset{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F)}{\ast} (L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}),E''\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. By uniqueness of the reduced C*-algebra of $E^r_{H\times F}$ we may and will view $C_r(\mathbb{G})\subset M$. Note that $C_r(\mathbb{G})''=M$ and $ E''\vert_{C_r(\mathbb{G})}= E^r_{H\times F}$. $(1)$ follows.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. Can be proved as statement $(3)$ in Theorem \ref{ThmReduced}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{PropModular}
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ one has $\varphi_\kappa=(h_H\otimes h_F)\circ\widetilde{\mathbb{E}}''_\kappa$ and, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$,
$$\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)}=\sigma_t^{\psi}\otimes \sigma_t^{h_G}\text{ and }\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}=\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_H}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_F}.$$

\item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ one has $h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}=\varphi_\kappa\circ\widetilde{E}_\kappa''$. In particular, $\sigma_t^{h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}}\vert_{L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}=\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.
\item For all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ one has $\varphi_\kappa=(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes h_\kappa)\circ\pi_\kappa''$ and $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}=\sigma_t^{h_\kappa}$
    \item For all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $\sigma_t^{h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}=\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}$. In particular, there exists a unique normal faithful conditional expectation $E_\mathbb{G}\,:\, {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\rightarrow{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ such that $h_{\mathbb{G}}\circ E_{\mathbb{G}}=h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
$(1)$ and $(2)$. The first equality follows from $\psi\circ E_\kappa=\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes h_H$ (Proposition \ref{PropUcpSection}). The equality about modular groups follows from Remark \ref{RmkModularFree} as well as statement $(2)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(3)$. Fix a system of matrix units $(e^\kappa_{ij})_{ij}$ in $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})$ diagonalizing $Q_\kappa$ i.e. $Q_\kappa e^\kappa_{ij}=\lambda_{k,i}e^\kappa_{ij}$. We note that $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})'\cap L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is generated by ${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\subset L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and $$\{\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)\,:\,1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa,\, a\in{\rm L}^\infty(G)\},\text{ where}$$ $\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a):=\sum_r(e^\kappa_{ri}\otimes 1\otimes 1)(1_B\otimes a)(e^\kappa_{jr}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\in L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. In particular, the linear span of $$\{x_0\rho^\kappa_{i_1j_1}(a_1)\dots\rho^\kappa_{i_nj_n}(a_n)x_n\,:\,n\geq 1, 1\leq i_s,j_s\leq N_\kappa,a_s\in{\rm L}^\infty(G),\,x_s\in{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\}$$ is a unital weakly dense $*$-subalgebra of $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$. Hence, it suffices to show that, for any $X$ of the form $X=x_0\rho^\kappa_{i_1j_1}(a_1)\dots\rho^\kappa_{i_nj_n}(a_n)x_n$ as above, one has $\varphi_\kappa(e^\kappa_{st}X)=\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})\varphi_\kappa(X)$, for all $1\leq s,t\leq N_\kappa$. Note that $e^\kappa_{st}X=(e^\kappa_{si_1}\otimes x_0)(1\otimes a_1)(e^\kappa_{j_1i_2}\otimes x_2)\dots(1\otimes a_n)(e^\kappa_{j_nt}\otimes x_n)$. Then,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\varphi_\kappa(e^\kappa_{st} X)&=&(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)\circ E_{\kappa,2}''(e^\kappa_{st}X)\\
&=&(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)\left( (e^\kappa_{si_1}\otimes x_0)E_{\kappa,2}''(X')(e^\kappa_{j_nt}\otimes x_n)\right)\\
&=&\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{si_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nt})=\frac{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1}e^\kappa_{si_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nt})}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}
=\frac{{\rm Tr}(e^\kappa_{j_nt}Q_\kappa^{-1}e^\kappa_{si_1}Y)}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}\\
&=&\frac{\delta_{s,t}\lambda_{\kappa,s}^{-1}{\rm Tr}(e^\kappa_{j_ni_1}Y)}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}=\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st}){\rm Tr}(e^\kappa_{j_ni_1}Y)
\end{eqnarray*}
where $X':=(1\otimes a_1)(e^\kappa_{j_1i_2}\otimes x_2)\dots(1\otimes a_n)$ and $$Y:=({\rm id}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)((1\otimes x_0)E_{\kappa,2}''(X')(1\otimes x_n)).$$
Note that $\psi_\kappa^{-1}\left(\sum_re^\kappa_{ri_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nr}\right)=(\psi_\kappa^{-1}\otimes h_H\otimes h_F)E''_{\kappa,2}(X)=\varphi_\kappa(X)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Writing $e^\kappa_{j_ni_1}=\frac{\sum_r\lambda_{\kappa,r}^{-1}e^\kappa_{j_nr}e^\kappa_{ri_1}}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}$ we get:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\varphi_\kappa(e^\kappa_{st}X)&=&\frac{\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}\sum_r\lambda_{\kappa,r}^{-1}{\rm Tr}(e^\kappa_{j_nr}e^\kappa_{ri_1}Y)=\frac{\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}\sum_r\lambda_{\kappa,r}^{-1}{\rm Tr}(e^\kappa_{ri_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nr})\\
&=&\frac{\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})}{{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1})}\sum_r{\rm Tr}(Q_\kappa^{-1}e^\kappa_{ri_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nr})=\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})\psi_\kappa^{-1}\left(\sum_re^\kappa_{ri_1}Ye^\kappa_{j_nr}\right)\\
&=&\psi_\kappa^{-1}(e^\kappa_{st})\varphi_\kappa(X).
\end{eqnarray*}

\noindent For the last part of $(3)$ we note that, under the identification $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}=\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\kappa}$ so, for all $x\in L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, $\sigma_t^{h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}}(x)=\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}(x)=(\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\kappa})(1\otimes x)=\sigma_t^{h_\kappa}(x)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}


\noindent$(4)$. Since for all $x\in L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, $(h_H\otimes h_F)\circ E''(x)=\varphi_\kappa(x)=h_\kappa(x)$, we deduce from general properties of the amalgamated free product that $\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}(x)=\sigma_t^{h_\kappa}(x)$. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is generated by the $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, for $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, it concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{CorKac}
$\mathbb{G}$ is Kac of and only if both $G$ and $H$ are Kac.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{PropScaling}
For all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))={\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, the scaling group of $\mathbb{G}$ is $\tau_t^\mathbb{G}=\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}$ and, $({\rm id}\otimes\tau_t^{\mathbb{G}})\rho=(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id})\rho\circ\tau_t^G$ and $({\rm id}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})\rho=(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id})\rho\circ\sigma_t^{h_G}$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{PropModular}, we note that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is generated by ${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ and $\{\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)\,:\,1\le\kappa\leq K,\,1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa,\,a\in {\rm L}^\infty(G)\}$. 
Since $H\times F$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$ one has, by definition of $\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}$, $\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}(x)=(\tau_t^H\otimes\tau_t^F)(x)=\tau_t^{\mathbb{G}}(x)$ for all $x\in{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. Moreover,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}(\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))&=&\widetilde{\tau}^\kappa_t(\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))=\sum_r(\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}(e^\kappa_{ri})\otimes 1\otimes 1)(1_B\otimes \tau_t^G(a))(\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}(e^\kappa_{jr})\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\sum_r\left(\frac{\lambda_{\kappa,i}}{\lambda_{\kappa,j}}\right)^{it}(e^\kappa_{ri}\otimes 1\otimes 1)(1_B\otimes \tau_t^G(a))(e^\kappa_{jr}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\\
&=&\left(\frac{\lambda_{\kappa,i}}{\lambda_{\kappa,j}}\right)^{it}\rho^\kappa_{ij}(\tau_t^G(a)).
\end{eqnarray*}
If follows that $\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))={\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. A similar computation gives
$$\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}(\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a))=\left(\frac{\lambda_{\kappa,i}}{\lambda_{\kappa,j}}\right)^{it}\rho^\kappa_{ij}(\sigma_t^{h_G}(a)).$$
It follows that $({\rm id}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})\rho=(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id})\rho\circ\tau_t^G$ and $({\rm id}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})\rho=(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id})\rho\circ\sigma_t^{h_G}$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textbf{Claim.} \textit{For all $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and all $X\in {\rm Pol}(G)\otimes B$ one has $\beta_G\circ(\tau_t^G\otimes\sigma_{-t}^\psi)(X)=(\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})\circ\beta_G(X)$.}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\begin{proof}[Proof of the Claim.] We may and will assume that $X=a\otimes b$, with $a\in{\rm Pol}(G)$ and $b\in B$. Then, using the computation above and Proposition \ref{PropQAut} $(2.c)$ we find:
\begin{align*}
\beta_G\circ(\tau_t^G\otimes\sigma_{-t}^\psi)(X)&=\rho(\tau_t^G(a))\beta(\sigma_{-t}^\psi(b))=(\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})(\rho(a))(\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_{t}^H)(\beta(b))\\
&=(\sigma^\psi_{-t}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})(\rho(a)\beta(b))=(\sigma^\psi_{-t}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})\circ\beta_G(a\otimes b).\qedhere
\end{align*}
\end{proof}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{End of the proof of Proposition \ref{PropScaling}.} To finish the proof, it suffices to show that, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, one has $\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}\circ\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}(x)=(\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})\circ\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}(x)$, for all $x\in{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ and all $x\in L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, $1\leq\kappa\leq K$. If $x\in{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ the equality is clear, since $H\times F$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$. Moreover, using the claim we find, for all $x\in{\rm Pol}(G)$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}}\circ\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})\rho(x)&=&({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}})(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id})\rho\circ\sigma_t^{h_G}(x)=(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\Delta_{\mathbb{G}})\rho(\sigma_t^{h_G}(x))\\
&=&(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho)\Delta_G(\sigma_t^{h_G}(x))\\
&=&(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho)(\tau_t^G\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G})\Delta_G(x)\\
&=&(\sigma_{t}^\psi\otimes{\rm id}\otimes{\rm id})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})(\tau_t^G\otimes\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\sigma_t^{h_{\mathbb{G}}})({\rm id}\otimes\rho)\Delta_G(x)\\
&=&({\rm id}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})(\beta_G\otimes{\rm id})({\rm id}\otimes\rho)\Delta_G\\
&=&({\rm id}\otimes({\rm id}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}})\Delta_{\mathbb{G}})\rho(x).
\end{eqnarray*}
It finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We may and will assume that $X=a\otimes b$, with $a\in{\rm Pol}(G)$ and $b\in B$. Then, using the computation above and Proposition \ref{PropQAut} $(2.c)$ we find:
\begin{align*}
\beta_G\circ(\tau_t^G\otimes\sigma_{-t}^\psi)(X)&=\rho(\tau_t^G(a))\beta(\sigma_{-t}^\psi(b))=(\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})(\rho(a))(\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_{t}^H)(\beta(b))\\
&=(\sigma^\psi_{-t}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})(\rho(a)\beta(b))=(\sigma^\psi_{-t}\otimes\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})\circ\beta_G(a\otimes b).\qedhere
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{rhofaith}
The map $\rho : {\rm L}^\infty(G)\rightarrow B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is faithful.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
We first remark that the map restricted to ${\rm Pol}(G)$ is faithful by the formula proved in Theorem \ref{TheoremErgodic}, $$ (\psi\otimes h_\mathbb{G}) \rho = h_G, $$ and the fact that all the states are faithful. Moreover, on ${\rm Pol}(G)$, it is defined as $$ \rho(a) = \sum_{\kappa,ij} e_{ij}^\kappa \otimes \sum_{s=1}^{N_\kappa}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{si}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{js}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\in B\otimes {\rm Pol}(\mathbb{G}),$$ therefore, the extension of $\rho$ to ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is also normal, and therefore the intertwining of the states still holds, and implies that $\rho$ is still faithful at the von Neumann algebraic level.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
One has $T^\tau(\mathbb{G}) = T^\tau(G)\cap T^\tau(H)$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Since $H$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, we get $T^\tau(\mathbb{G})\subset T^\tau(H)$ and, using the formulas $\tau^H_t(u^{ij,\kappa}_{kk,\gamma}) = \left(\dfrac{\lambda_{\kappa,i}}{\lambda_{\kappa,j}} \right)^{it}u_{kk,\gamma}^{ij,\kappa}$ and $\sigma_t^\psi(b^\kappa_{ij})=\left(\frac{\lambda_{\kappa,i}}{\lambda_{\kappa,j}}\right)^{it}$ we deduce that $T^\tau(H)\subset B^\psi$, where $B^\psi$ denotes the centralizer of $\psi$. Fix $t\in T^\tau(\mathbb{G})$ then $\sigma_t^\psi={\rm id}$ and,
$$\rho =({\rm id}\otimes \tau^\mathbb{G}_t)\rho = (\sigma_t^\psi\otimes {\rm id})\rho\circ \tau_t^G = \rho\circ\tau_t^G. $$ From this we get that $\tau_t^G={\rm id}$ by faithfulness of the map $\rho$. Therefore $T^\tau(\mathbb{G}) \subset T^\tau(G)\cap T^\tau(H)$.
Assume now that $t \in T^\tau(G)\cap T^\tau(H)$, then $t\in B^\psi$ and, using that $({\rm id}\otimes \tau^\mathbb{G}_t)\rho = (\sigma_t^\psi\otimes {\rm id})\rho\circ \tau_t^G = \rho$, we get that $\tau_t^\mathbb{G}$ is trivial on the coefficients of $\rho$. Since $t\in T^\tau(H)$ we deduce that $\tau_t^\mathbb{G}={\rm id}$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
\label{rmk fd amal}
View ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=\underset{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}{*}(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))\underset{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))$, where the inclusion maps and the conditional expectations are the ones described before. Let us denote by $\nu_\kappa\,:\, B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)\rightarrow{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and $\mu_\kappa\,:\,M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\rightarrow{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$, $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, the canonical inclusions. We also write $\mu\,:\,{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\rightarrow{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$, $\mu(x):=\mu_\kappa(1\otimes x)$ for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ and all $x\in{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. Let $M\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ be the von Neumann subalgebra defined by:
$$M_0:=\left\{\mu_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))\,:\,1\leq\kappa\leq K\right\}''.$$
Remark that $$M_0 \simeq (\ast_\kappa M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C}),\psi_\kappa^{-1})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F).$$
Then we define inductively the algebras $$M_{\kappa} := \left( M_{\kappa-1} \cup \nu_\kappa(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)) \right)''\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}),$$
for any $1\leq \kappa \leq K$.
Note that, by uniqueness of amalgamated free product of von Neumann algebras, one has that $$ M_{\kappa} \simeq M_{\kappa-1} \ast_{B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F)} \nu_\kappa(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)), $$
where the amalgamated free products are with respect to the maps $\beta_\kappa\otimes {\rm id}_F$ and the obvious corresponding conditional expectations. This also shows that we have
$${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\simeq M_K.$$ 
Observe that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is the von Neumann subalgebra generated by
$$\{\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a)\,:\,1\leq\kappa\leq K,1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa,a\in{\rm L}^\infty(G)\}\cup\mu({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)),$$where $\rho^\kappa_{ij}(a):=\sum_{r=1}^{N_\kappa}\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{ri}\otimes 1\otimes 1)\nu_\kappa(1\otimes a)\mu_\kappa(e^\kappa_{jr}\otimes 1\otimes 1)$.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thmAtxt}
The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ has the Haagerup property then both $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ have the Haagerup property. If moreover ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite, then $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ has the Haagerup property if and only if both $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ have the Haagerup property.
    \item Assume that $\mathbb{G}$ is Kac (so that both $G$ and $H$ are Kac). If $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ is hyperlinear then both $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ are hyperlinear. Moreover, if ${\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is amenable, then $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ is hyperlinear if and only if both $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ are hyperlinear.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
\noindent$(1)$. Assume that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ has the Haagerup property. Since $H$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ is a subalgebra with expectation, by Lemma \ref{dualqsg}. Therefore ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ has the Haagerup approximation property. By the decomposition of ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ as a free product, we get for any $\kappa$ a faithful conditional expectation onto the algebra $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, which implies that the algebra $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ and therefore $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C}) \otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})=L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ have the Haagerup approximation property. Since there is a conditional expectation $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}) \rightarrow (B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(G))$, $B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(G)$ has the Haagerup property, and therefore $\widehat{G}$ has it too.
For the converse, assume that ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite and that $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ have the Haagerup property, then we can apply \cite[Corollary 8.2]{CKSVW21} to the decomposition of ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ as an inductive amalgamated free product over $B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F)$ as described in Remark \ref{rmk fd amal}. First, we remark that by the result of \cite[Corollary 8.2]{CKSVW21}, the algebra $\ast_\kappa( M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C}),\psi_\kappa^{-1})$ has the Haagerup property and therefore, if $\widehat{H}$ has the Haagerup approximation property, then so does $M_0$. Moreover if $\widehat{G}$ has the Haagerup property, then so does $B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(G)$, and an induction shows that $M_K \simeq {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ has the Haagerup property. Finally, using the conditional expectation $ {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}) \rightarrow {\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we get that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ has the Haagerup property.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. We already know thanks to Proposition \ref{CorKac} that $\mathbb{G}$ is Kac if and only $G$ and $H$ are Kac. Under these condition, $h_G, h_H,\psi,h_\mathbb{G}$ are all traces.  Assume first that $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ is hyperlinear then, as $H$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, $\widehat{H}$ is also hyperlinear. Note that $B$ being finite dimensional $(B,\psi)$ is Connes embeddable (CE). Hence, $(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}),\psi\otimes h_\mathbb{G})$ also is, by \cite{Pop95}. Since the map $\rho\,:\,{\rm L}^\infty(G)\rightarrow B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is faithful and satisfies $(\psi\otimes h_\mathbb{G})\rho=h_G$, $\widehat{G}$ is hyperlinear. Conversely, assume that both $\widehat{G}$ and $\widehat{H}$ are hyperlinear and ${\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is amenable. Then, \cite[Corollary 4.5]{BDJ08} implies that $*_\kappa(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C}),\psi_\kappa^{-1})$ is CE hence, $M_0$ is CE. Applying \cite[Corollary 4.5]{BDJ08} (and since ${\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is amenable) inductively in Remark \ref{rmk fd amal}, we deduce that $({\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}),h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}})$ is CE. Since the inclusion ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is state preserving, we deduce that $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}$ is hyperlinear.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{LemZ3}
Let $H$ be a CQG. If $\vert{\rm Irr}(H)\vert=3$ then $H\simeq\mathbb{Z}_3$ or $H\simeq S_3$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Write ${\rm Irr}(H)=\{1,x_1,x_2\}$, where $x_1\neq x_2$ are non-trivial irreducibles. Since $x_1$ is non-trivial we have either $\overline{x}_1=x_1$ or $\overline{x}_1=x_2$. Assume that $\overline{x}_1=x_1$, so that $\overline{x}_2=x_2$. Hence, $\mathrm{Mor}(1,x_1\otimes x_2)=0$ and it follows that there exists $n_1,n_2\geq 0$ such that $x_1\otimes x_2=n_1x_1+n_2x_2$. Also, $\dim\mathrm{Mor}(1,x_k\otimes x_k)=1$, $\dim\mathrm{Mor}(x_1,x_2\otimes x_2)=\dim\mathrm{Mor}(x_2,x_1\otimes x_2)=n_2$ and $\dim\mathrm{Mor}(x_2,x_1\otimes x_1)=\dim\mathrm{Mor}(x_1,x_1\otimes x_2)=n_1$. Hence, there exists $s,t\geq 0$ such that $x_1\otimes x_1=1+ sx_1+n_1x_2$ and $x_2\otimes x_2=1+n_2x_1+tx_2$. It follows that $d_1^2=1+sd_1+n_1d_2$ and $d_2^2=1+n_2d_1+td_2$, where $d_k:=\dim(x_k)$. In particular, ${\rm gcd}(d_1,d_2)=1$. Note that $(n_1,n_2)$ is a solution to the Diophantine equation $d_1d_2=n_1d_1+n_2d_2$ and since ${\rm gcd}(d_1,d_2)=1$ and $n_1,n_2\geq 0$ we deduce that $(n_1,n_2)\in\{(d_2,0),(0,d_1)\}$. Assume that $n_1=d_2$ and $n_2=0$. Then, $d_1^2=1+sd_1+d_2^2$ and $d_2^2=1+td_2$. From the equation $d_2^2-td_2-1=0$ we deduce that $\Delta_2:=t^2+4$ is a perfect square, which happens if and only if $t=0$. We conclude that $d_2=1$. From the equation $d_1^2-sd_1-2=0$ we deduce that $\Delta_1:=s^2+8$ is a perfect square, which happens if and only if $s=1$. Hence, $d_1=2$. It follows that $\dim(C(H))=1+d_1^2+d_2^2=6$. Assuming now that $n_1=0$ and $n_2=d_1$, the same proof, exchanging the role of $x_1$ and $x_2$ also shows that $\dim(C(H))=6$. However, the only compact quantum groups whose associated C*-algebras have dimension $6$ are $\mathbb{Z}_6$, $S_3 \simeq \mathbb{Z}_3\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and its dual $\widehat{S_3}$. $\mathbb{Z}_6$ and $\widehat{S_3}$ both have $6$ irreducibles, each of dimension $1$, and therefore $H \simeq S_3$. It remains to check the other case, that is $\overline{x}_1=x_2$ and $\overline{x}_2=x_1$. Let $s,t\geq 0$ be such that $x_2\otimes x_1=1+tx_1+sx_2$ and write $d=\dim(x_1)=\dim(x_2)$. 
Hence, $d^2=1+(t+s)d$ and, this implies that $1=0$ modulo $d$ so $d=1$ and $x_2\otimes x_1=1$. Letting $u\in\mathcal{U}(C(H))$ the group like unitary $u:=x_1\neq 1$ we have $u^*=x_2\neq u$ so $u^3=1$ and we deduce that $H=\mathbb{Z}_3$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{LemZ2} Let $p\geq 2$ be a integer. The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p$ is prime.
\item $\mathbb{Z}_p$ has, up to isomorphism, exactly 2 ergodic actions on a finite dimensional C*-algebra $B$:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $B\simeq\mathbb{C}$ and $\beta$ is the trivial action,
    \item $B\simeq\mathbb{C}^p$ and $\beta$ is isomorphic to the action $\mathbb{Z}_p\curvearrowright C^*(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ by left translation.
    \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
$(1)\Rightarrow(2)$. View $\beta\,:\,\mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow{\rm Aut}(B)\subset\mathcal{L}(B)$ and write $\mathbb{Z}_p=\langle\sigma\rangle$ where $\sigma^p=1$. Hence $\beta(\sigma)^p={\rm id}_B$ so ${\rm Sp}(\beta(\sigma))\subseteq\{\xi^k\,:\, 0\leq k\leq p-1\}$, where $\xi=e^{2i\pi/p}$ and we may write $B=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{p-1}B_k$ as vector spaces, where $B_k=\{b\in B:\beta(\sigma)b=\xi^kb\}$. Since $\beta$ is ergodic we have $B_0=\mathbb{C} 1_B$. Note that $B_k^*=B_{-k}$ and $B_kB_l\subset B_{k+l}$, where the sum is modulo $p$. If $B_{1}\neq\{0\}$, take a nonzero $a\in B_{1}$. Then, $a^*a\in B_0=\mathbb{C}1$ and is non-zero. Let $\lambda\neq 0$ be such that $a^*a=\lambda1$. Take $\lambda^{-1/2}$ be any square root of $\lambda^{-1}$ and define $u:=\lambda^{-1/2}a$. Then $u$ satisfies $u^*u=1_B$ and, since $B$ is finite dimensional, we also have $uu^*=1$. Note that, for any $1\leq k\leq p-1$, any $b\in B_{k}$, one has $b(u^{k})^*\in B_kB_{-k}\subset B_0=\mathbb{C}1_B$ which implies that $B_{k}=\mathbb{C} u^{k}$. We also have $u^p\in (B_1)^p\subset B_0=\mathbb{C}1$. Hence, up to replacing $u$ by a modulus one multiple of $u$, we may and will assume that $u^p=1$.
