Hence, the unique map $C^*(\mathbb{Z}_p)\rightarrow B=\bigoplus_{k=0}^{p-1}\mathbb{C} u^k$ which map $\sigma$ onto $u$ is an isomorphism intertwining the left translation on $C^*(\mathbb{Z}_p)$ with the action $\beta$. Assume now that $B_1=\{0\}$. Fix $2\leq k\leq p-1$ and assume that $B_k\neq 0$. Let $a\in B_k$ be non-zero and, as before, we may further assume by ergodicity that $a^*a=aa^*=1$. Then, by Fermat's Little Theorem, $a^{k^{p-1}-1}\in B_k^{k^{p-1}-1}\subset B_{k^{p-1}}=B_1=\{0\}$. Hence, $a^{p^{k-1}-1}=0$ and $a^*=(a^*)^{p^{k-1}}a^{p^{k-1}-1}=0$ so $a=0$ a contradiction. We deduce that $B_k=0$ for all $1\leq k\leq p-1$. So $B=\mathbb{C}1$ and $\beta$ is the trivial action.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)\Rightarrow(1)$. if $p>2$ is not prime write $p=nm$ with $n,m\geq 2$ and consider the ergodic action $\mathbb{Z}_n\curvearrowright \mathbb{C}^n=C^*(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ by left translation. Then, composing with the canonical surjection $\mathbb{Z}_p\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_n$ sending the generator of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ on the generator of $\mathbb{Z}_n$, we get an ergodic action $\mathbb{Z}_p\curvearrowright\mathbb{C}^n$. However, this action is not faithful so it can not be isomorphic to the left translation of $\mathbb{Z}_p$, which is faithful.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{LemS3}
There are, up to isomorphism, exactly $4$ ergodic actions of $\widehat{S_3}$ on a finite dimensional C*-algebra $B$:
\begin{itemize}
    \item The trivial action $\beta_1$ on $B=\mathbb{C}$;
    \item The ergodic action $\beta_2\,:\,\mathbb{C}^2\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^2\otimes C(\mathbb{Z}_2)\subset \mathbb{C}^2\otimes C^*(S_3)$ on $B=\mathbb{C}^2$ coming from the unique ergodic action of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ on $\mathbb{C}^2$.
    \item The ergodic action $\beta_3\,:\,\mathbb{C}^3\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^3\otimes C(\mathbb{Z}_3)\subset \mathbb{C}^3\otimes C^*(S_3)$ on $B=\mathbb{C}^3$ coming from the unique ergodic action of $\mathbb{Z}_3$ on $\mathbb{C}^3$.
    \item The ergodic action $\beta_4:=\Delta_{\widehat{S_3}}\,:\,C^*(S_3)\rightarrow C^*(S_3)\otimes C^*(S_3)$ on $B=C^*(S_3)$ given by the comultiplication.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Write $B=B_1\oplus B_\sigma\oplus B_{\sigma^2}\oplus B_\tau\oplus B_{\tau\sigma}\oplus B_{\sigma\tau}$, where $B_g:=\{b\in B\,:\,\beta(b)=b\otimes g\}$. The order $2$ elements are $\{\tau,\tau\sigma,\sigma\tau\}$. Note that $A_\sigma:=B_1\oplus B_\sigma\oplus B_{\sigma^2}$ is a subalgebra of $B$ and $\beta(A_\sigma)\subset A_\sigma\otimes C^*(\sigma)$ so we get an ergodic action $\mathbb{Z}_3\curvearrowright A_\sigma$. Similarly, for any order two element $\omega\in\{\sigma,\tau\sigma,\sigma\tau\}$, $A_\omega:=B_1\oplus B_\omega$ is a subalgebra with an ergodic action $\mathbb{Z}_2\curvearrowright A_\omega$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Assume first that $\mathbb{Z}_3\curvearrowright A_\sigma$ is ergodic then there is an element $u\in B_\sigma$ such that $u^3=1$ and $B_\sigma=\mathbb{C} u$, $B_{\sigma^2}=\mathbb{C} u^2$. Now, if for some $\omega\in\{\tau,\sigma\tau,\tau\sigma\}$ the action $\mathbb{Z}_2\curvearrowright A_\omega$ is also ergodic then we have $B_\tau=\mathbb{C} v$ with some $v$ satisfying $v^2=1$. Since $B_gB_h\subset B_{gh}$ and $\langle\sigma,\omega\rangle=S_3$ we deduce that $B_g\neq\{0\}$ for all $g\in S_3$. It follows that $\dim(B)=6$ and $\beta$ is isomorphic to $\beta_4$. If now $\mathbb{Z}_2\curvearrowright A_\omega$ is trivial for all $\omega\in \{\tau,\tau\sigma,\sigma\tau\}$. It follows that $\dim(B)=3$ and $\beta$ is isomorphic to $\beta_3$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Assume now that $\mathbb{Z}_3\curvearrowright A_\sigma$ is the trivial action. Since for any $\omega_1,\omega_2\in\{\tau,\tau\sigma,\sigma\tau\}$ with $\omega_1\neq\omega_2$ we have $\langle\omega_1,\omega_2\rangle=S_3$ and since $B_\sigma=\{0\}$, there at most one $\omega\in\{\tau,\sigma\tau,\tau\sigma\}$ such that $\mathbb{Z}^3\curvearrowright B_\omega$ is nontrivial. If there is such a $\omega$ then $\beta$ is isomorphic to $\beta_2$ and if there is no such $\omega$ then $\beta$ is the trivial action $\beta_1$ on $B=\mathbb{C}$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{PropCoamenable}
Assume that $F$ is trivial and both $G$ and $H$ are non-trivial then the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\mathbb{G}$ is coamenable.
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is amenable.
    \item $G\simeq H\simeq \mathbb{Z}_2$ and $B\in\{\mathbb{C},\mathbb{C}^2\}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case we have either $\mathbb{G}=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2}}$ or $\mathbb{G}=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2}}\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
$(1)\Rightarrow(2)$ follows from the general theory \cite{To06}.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent $(2)\Rightarrow(3)$. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is amenable,  each  $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ is amenable. Write $C=B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)$ and $D=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)$ so that $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=C\underset{B}{*}D$. Let $p:=e^\gamma_{jj}\in B$ be a minimal projection and note that $\sigma_t^\psi(p)=p$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Let us show that $pCp={\rm L}^\infty(G)$ and $pDp=\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p)$ are $*$-free in $pL_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})p$ with respect to the state $\omega:=(\varphi_\kappa(p))^{-1}\varphi_\kappa(p\cdot p)$. Let $x\in pL_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}) p$ be a word alternating from $pCp$ and $pDp$ of the form $x=(pc_1p)(pd_1p)\dots (pc_np)(pd_np)$, with $c_k\in C$, $d_k\in D$ and $\omega(pc_kp)=\omega(pd_kp)=0$. Since $p\in B$ is a minimal projection, we have for $e_k\in\{c_k,d_k\}$, $E_B(pe_k p)=pE_B(e_k)p\in\mathbb{C}1_B$. Hence, $E_B(pe_k p)=\psi(E_B(pe_kp))1_B=\varphi_\kappa(pe_kp)1_B=0$. It follows that $x$ is a reduced operator in the amalgamated free product $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=C\underset{B}{*}D$. Hence, $\varphi_\kappa(x)=0=\psi(p)\omega(x)$ so $\omega(x)=0$. One proves similarly that $\omega(x)=0$ for other alternating products $x$. This shows that $pCp*pDp\simeq\langle pCp,pDp\rangle\subset p L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}) p $, where the free product is with respect to the state $\omega$. Note that, since $p\in B^\psi\subset (L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))^{\varphi_\kappa}$, one has $\sigma_t^\omega(pxp)=p\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}(x)p$, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $x\in L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. In particular, $\sigma^\omega_t(pCp)=pCp$ and $\sigma^\omega_t(pDp)=pDp$. Hence, $\sigma_t^\omega(\langle pCp,pDp\rangle)=\langle pCp,pDp\rangle$ and, by Takesaki's Theorem, the subalgebra $\langle pCp,pDp\rangle\subset p L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})p$ has a faithful normal conditional expectation. Hence, $pCp*pDp={\rm L}^\infty(G)*\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p)$ is amenable. Note that if ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ is infinite dimensional, then ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ is diffuse by \cite[Lemma 2.4]{FT24}. Hence, $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)$ is also diffuse and $\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p)$ must be infinite dimensional. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(G)\neq\mathbb{C}$, the results of \cite{Ue10} imply that $pCp*pDp$ is not amenable. Hence, ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ is finite dimensional. Let $q_x$ be the minimal central projections of ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$, which are parameterized by $x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})$ and note that $\varepsilon_H(a)q_1=aq_1$ for all $a\in C(H)$, where $1\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})$ is the trivial representation. Note that $$\dim(\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p))\geq 2.$$
Indeed, if the dimension is $1$, then $\beta_\kappa(p)$ is a minimal projection and it implies that $\beta_\kappa(p)(1_\kappa\otimes p_1)=\beta_\kappa(p)$. Hence,
$$\beta_\kappa(p)=\beta_\kappa(p)(1_\kappa\otimes p_1)=({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_H)(\beta_\kappa(p)(1_\kappa\otimes p_1))=\chi_\kappa(p)\otimes p_1=\delta_{\gamma,\kappa}(p\otimes p_1).$$
Since $\beta_\kappa$ is faithful, we deduce that $K=1$ and $\beta(p)=p\otimes p_1$. Applying $\psi\otimes{\rm id}$ we get $\psi(p)1=\psi(p)p_1$ so $p_1=1$ and $H$ is trivial, a contradiction.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Since $pCp,pDp\neq\mathbb{C}$ and $pCp*pDp$ is amenable, the results of \cite{Ue10} imply that:
$$\dim({\rm L}^\infty(G))\leq 2\text{ and }\dim(\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p))\leq 2.$$
We deduce that $\dim({\rm L}^\infty(G))= 2=\dim(\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p))$ which implies that $G\simeq\mathbb{Z}_2$. Hence both $G$ and $H$ are Kac, by \cite[Theorem 2.2]{VD97}. Hence, $\mathbb{G}$ is Kac and, since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is amenable and $\mathbb{G}$ is Kac, \cite{To06} implies that $\mathbb{G}$ is amenable so $G^{*K}$, as a compact quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, is also amenable. \cite[Proposition 2.8]{FT24} implies that $K\leq 2$. Write $$\beta(p)=\sum_{x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})}\beta(p)(1\otimes q_x).$$
Write, for $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, $I_\kappa:=\{x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H}):\beta_\kappa(p)(1\otimes q_x)\neq 0\}$ and note that, since $(q_x)$ are central and pairwise orthogonal, $\{\beta_\kappa(p)(1\otimes q_x):x\in I_\kappa\}$ is a family of non-zero pairwise orthogonal projections in $\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p)$. Hence,
$$\vert I_\kappa\vert\leq\dim(\beta_\kappa(p)(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(H))\beta_\kappa(p))= 2\text{ for all }1\leq\kappa\leq K.$$
Note that ${\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})= \cup_{\kappa=1}^K I_\kappa$. Indeed, writing $I:=\{x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H}):\beta(p)(1\otimes p_x)\neq 0\}$ one has:
 $$\psi(p)1=(\psi\otimes{\rm id})(\beta(p))=\sum_{x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})}(\psi\otimes{\rm id})(\beta(p)(1\otimes q_x))=\sum_{x\in I}\psi(p)q_x.$$
 Since $\psi(p)>0$ it follows that $\sum_{x\in I}p_x=1$ so $I={\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})$. Let $x\in{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})$, since $\beta(p)(1\otimes q_x)\neq 0$, there exists $\kappa$ such that $x\in I_\kappa$ and this shows that ${\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})= \cup_{\kappa=1}^K I_\kappa$.
 
\vspace{0.2cm}
 
\noindent If $K=1$ this shows that $\vert{\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})\vert=2$. Arguing as in the proof of \cite[Proposition 2.8]{FT24}, we deduce that $\widehat{H}\simeq \mathbb{Z}_2$. Hence, $H\simeq\widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2}\simeq\mathbb{Z}_2$.
 
\vspace{0.2cm}
 
\noindent If $K=2$. Since $({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_H)\beta={\rm id}_B$, the trivial representation $1$ is in $I_1\cap I_2$. Hence, $\vert {\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})\vert=\vert I_1\vert+\vert I_2\vert-\vert I_1\cap I_2\vert\leq \vert I_1\vert+\vert I_2\vert -1\leq 3$ so either $\vert {\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})\vert=2$ in which case we deduce again that $H=\mathbb{Z}_2$ or $\vert {\rm Irr}(\widehat{H})\vert=3$ and Lemma \ref{LemZ3} implies that $\widehat{H}\in\{\mathbb{Z}_3,S_3\}$ so $H\in\{\mathbb{Z}_3,\widehat{S}_3\}$. In conclusion, we have $G=\mathbb{Z}_2$ and either $K=1$ and $H=\mathbb{Z}_2$ or $K=2$ and $H\in\{\mathbb{Z}_2,\mathbb{Z}_3,\widehat{S_3}\}$. However, in the case $K=2$ and $H=\mathbb{Z}_3$, there is no ergodic action of $\mathbb{Z}_3$ on $B$, by Lemma \ref{LemZ2}. If $K=2$ and $H=\widehat{S_3}$ then, by Lemma \ref{LemS3} we have $B=\mathbb{C}^2$ and $\beta$ is the action $\mathbb{C}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{C}^2\otimes C(\mathbb{Z}_2)=\mathbb{C}^2\otimes C^*(\omega)\subset\mathbb{C}^2\otimes C^*(S_3)$ coming from the unique ergodic action of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ on $\mathbb{C}^2$ and an order two element $\omega\in S_3$. We deduce from Proposition \ref{Propfaithful} that $\mathbb{G}\simeq (\mathbb{Z}_2\wr_{*}\mathbb{Z}_2)\underset{\mathbb{Z}_2}{*}\widehat{S_3}$. By Proposition \ref{PropBichon} and \cite[Proposition 2.23]{FT24} we have $\mathbb{Z}_2\wr_{*}\mathbb{Z}_2\simeq \widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2}}\rtimes \mathbb{Z}_2$. Hence, ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=({\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})\otimes{\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2))\underset{{\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2)}{*}{\rm L}(S_3)$, where the amalgamated free product is with respect to the conditional expectations on the dual quantum subgroup $\mathbb{Z}_2$. Write $S_3=\langle\sigma,\tau\vert\sigma^3=1,\tau^2=1,\tau\sigma\tau=\sigma^{-1}\rangle$ and let $p:=\frac{1}{2}(1+\tau)\in{\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2)$ and note that $p=p^*=p^2$ and $p\tau=p$ so $p$ is a minimal projection in ${\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2)$. However, $p$ is not minimal in ${\rm L}(S_3)$ since $p{\rm L}(S_3)p=\mathbb{C} p\oplus\mathbb{C} p\sigma p$. It is easy to check that ${\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})=p({\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})\otimes{\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2))p$ and $p{\rm L}(S_3)p$ are $*$-free in $p{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ with respect to $h_\mathbb{G}(p)^{-1}h_\mathbb{G}\vert_{p{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}$. Hence, ${\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})*p{\rm L}(S_3)p$ is isomorphic to a von Neumann algebra of $p{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ which is impossible since ${\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})$ is diffuse and $\dim(p{\rm L}(S_3)p)\geq 2$ so ${\rm L}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2})*p{\rm L}(S_3)p$ is not amenable. It follows that the only possible case is $G=H=\mathbb{Z}_2$ and Lemma \ref{LemZ2} implies that $B\in\{\mathbb{C},\mathbb{C}^2\}$.
 
\vspace{0.2cm}
 
\noindent $(3)\Rightarrow(1)$. If $G=H=\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $B=\mathbb{C}$ then $\beta$ is the trivial action on $\mathbb{C}$ and it follows from Remark  \ref{RmkFwp} that $\mathbb{G}\simeq\widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2}}$ which is coamenable. If $B=\mathbb{C}^2$ then Lemma \ref{LemZ2} implies that $\beta$ is the unique ergodic action on $B=\mathbb{C}^2$ so that it is isomorphic to the universal action $\mathbb{Z}_2=S_2^+\curvearrowright\mathbb{C}^2$. Proposition \ref{PropBichon} and \cite[Proposition 2.23]{FT24} imply that $\mathbb{G}\simeq\widehat{\mathbb{Z}_2^{*2}}\rtimes \mathbb{Z}_2$, which is coamenable by \cite[Proposition 2.17]{FT24}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
The fact that, for $G$ a CQG of Kac type, the coamenability of $G$ is equivalent to the amenability of the von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is well known (see Corollary 3.17 in \cite{To06} and the discussion after its proof) and was used in the previous proof. However, the equivalence for general CQG is open. Theorem \ref{PropCoamenable} shows that in the class of CQG which are non-amalgamated generalized free wreath product of non-trivial CQG with ergodic action, the equivalence between coamenability and amenability of the von Neumann algebra is true. Since this class of CQG contains in particular the class of free products of non-trivial CQG, it extends \cite[Remark 2.9]{FT24}.
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
The ergodicity is necessary to obtain $(1)\Rightarrow (2)$ in Theorem \ref{PropCoamenable}. Indeed, consider the free action $\mathbb{Z}_2\curvearrowright\mathbb{Z}_2$ and let $B=M_N(\mathbb{C})$ with $N\geq 2$ and $B^{\mathbb{Z}_2}=M_N(\mathbb{C})\oplus M_N(\mathbb{C})$ with the action $\beta\,:\,\mathbb{Z}_2\curvearrowright B^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ defined before Proposition \ref{PropSemiDirect}. This action is non-ergodic and preserves the faithful state $\psi$ defined from any faithful state $\omega\in M_N(\mathbb{C})^*$ before Proposition \ref{PropSemiDirect}. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be the free wreath product $\mathbb{G}:=G\wr_{*,\beta}\mathbb{Z}_2$. Note that, by Proposition \ref{PropSemiDirect}, $\mathbb{G}\simeq G^{*2}\rtimes \mathbb{Z}_2$. Hence, $\mathbb{G}$ is coamenable if and only if $G$ is trivial or $G=\mathbb{Z}_2$, by \cite[Propositions 2.8 and 2.17]{FT24}. Hence, taking $G=H=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we obtain a coamenable free wreath product $\mathbb{G}$ but with $B=M_N(\mathbb{C})\oplus M_N(\mathbb{C})$.
<!-- end remark-19 -->
<!-- remark-20: body_md -->
\label{RmkExp}
If $A\subset M$ is with expectation then its relative commutant $A'\cap M$, the von Neumann algebra $A\vee (A'\cap M)\subset M$ generated by $A$ and $A'\cap M$ and its normalizer algebra $\mathcal{N}_M(A)''\subset M$, where $\mathcal{N}_M(A):=\{v\in\mathcal{U}(M)\,:\,vAv^*=A\}$, are all with expectation. Indeed, fix a faithful normal conditional expectation $E_A\,:\, M\rightarrow A$, fix a f.n.s. $\psi\in A_*$ and define the f.n.s. $\psi\in M_*$ by $\psi:=\psi\circ E_A$. Since $A$ is globally invariant under the modular group $\sigma_t^\psi$, it is easy to see that $A'\cap M$ also is. It implies that $A\vee (A'\cap M)$ is globally invariant under $\sigma_t^\psi$. Moreover, it is shown in \cite[Lemma 4.1]{BHV18} that, for all $u\in\mathcal{N}_M(A)$ and all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, one has $$u^*\sigma_t(u)\in A\vee (A'\cap M)\subset\mathcal{N}_M(A)'',$$
In particular, $\mathcal{N}_M(A)''$ is globally invariant under $\sigma_t^\psi$. It follows from Takesaki's Theorem that there exists a unique $\psi$-preserving conditional expectation from $M$ to $A'\cap M$, from $M$ to $A\vee (A'\cap M)$ and from $M$ to $\mathcal{N}_M(A)''$, these conditional expectations are moreover normal and faithful.
<!-- end remark-20 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{DefEmbedds}
Let $A\subset 1_AM1_A$ and $B\subset 1_BM1_B$ be von Neumann subalgebras with expectation. We say that $A$ \textit{embeds in} $B$ \textit{inside} $M$ and we write $A\prec_M B$ if there exist projections $e\in A$, $f\in B$ a non-zero element $v\in eMf$ and a unital, normal $*$-morphism $\theta : eAe \rightarrow fBf$ such that the inclusion $\theta(eAe)\subset fBf$ is with expectation and $av = v\theta(a)$ for all $a\in eAe$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- remark-21: body_md -->
\label{RmkEmbedds} Let $A\subset 1_AM1_A$ and $B\subset 1_BM1_B$ be von Neumann subalgebras with expectations.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A$ is diffuse and $B$ is finite dimensional then $A\nprec_M B$. Indeed, assume that $A\prec_M B$, it follows from \cite[Remark 4.2 (3)]{HI17} that there exist projections $e\in A$, $f\in B$, a non-zero element $v\in eMf$ and a \textit{faithful} unital normal $*$-homomorphism $\theta\,:\,eAe\rightarrow fBf$ such that $av=v\theta(a)$ for all $a\in eAe$. If $B=\mathbb{C}1_B$ then, since $\theta$ is faithful, $eAe=\mathbb{C} e$ and $e$ is minimal. In general, since $fBf$ is finite dimensional and $v\in eMf$, there exists a minimal (and central) projection $q\in fBf$ such that $vq\neq 0$. Consider $w=vq\in eMq$ and $\psi\,:\, eAe\rightarrow qBq=\mathbb{C} q$, $\psi(a)=\theta(a)q=q\theta(a)$. Then, $w\psi(a)=vq\theta(a)=v\theta(a)q=avq=aw$. Hence, $A\prec_M\mathbb{C}$ and we can apply the first part of the proof.
\item Let $p\in\mathcal{Z}(M)$ be a projection. Then, $Ap\subset 1_AMp1_A$ and $Bp\subset 1_BMp1_B$ are with expectation and if $Ap\prec_{Mp}Bp$ then $A\prec_MB$ (see \cite[Remark 4.2 (2)]{HI17}). 

\item $A\prec_M B$ if and only if $A\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})\prec_{M\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})} B\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})$ for some $k\geq 1$ (or for any $k\geq 1$). Indeed, assume that for some $k\geq 1$ one has $\mathcal{A}\prec_\mathcal{M} \mathcal{B}$, where $\mathcal{A}:=A\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})$, $\mathcal{B}:=B\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathcal{M}:=M\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})$ and consider the projection $p:=1_A\otimes e_{11}\in \mathcal{A}$. Note that its central support in $\mathcal{A}$ is $z_{\mathcal{A}}(1_A\otimes e_{11})=1_A\otimes 1$. It follows from \cite[Remark 4.2 (4)]{HI17} that $p\mathcal{A}p=A\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}\prec_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{B}$. The same argument, by using this time \cite[Remark 4.5]{HI17}, shows that $A\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}\prec_{\mathcal{M}} B\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}$. Hence, there exist projections $e\in A$, $f\in B$, a non-zero $w\in (e\otimes e_{11})(M\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C}))(f\otimes e_{11})=eMf\otimes \mathbb{C} e_{11}$ and a unital normal $*$-homomorphism $\psi\,:\,eAe\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}\rightarrow fBf\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}$ such that $\psi(eAe\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11})\subset fBf\otimes\mathbb{C} e_{11}$ is with expectation and $(a\otimes e_{11})w=w\psi(a\otimes e_{11})$ for all $a\in eAe$. Let $\theta\,:\,eAe\rightarrow fBf$ be the unique unital normal $*$-homomorphism such that $\psi(a\otimes e_{11})=\theta(a)\otimes e_{11}$ for all $a\in eAe$ and $v\in eMf$ be the unique (non-zero) element such that $w=v\otimes e_{11}$. Then $\theta(eAe)\subset fBf$ is with expectation and $av=v\theta(a)$ for all $a\in eAe$. For the converse, it is clear from Definition \ref{DefEmbedds} that $A\prec_MB$ implies $A\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})\prec_{M\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})} B\otimes M_k(\mathbb{C})$ for all $k\geq 1$.
\item If $A\prec_MB$ then, for any \textit{unital} $D\subset A$ with expectation one has $D\prec_M B$ by \cite[Lemma 4.8]{HI17}.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-21 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 4.3 and Lemma 4.10]{HI17}\label{HI17thm}
Let $A\subset 1_AM1_A$ and $B\subset 1_BM1_B$ with expectations and suppose that $A$ is finite or type ${\rm III}$. Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $A\prec_M B$.
    \item There exist $n\geq 1$, a projection $q\in M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes B$, a non-zero partial isometry $w\in (e_{11}\otimes 1_A)(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M)q$ and a unital normal $*$-homomorphism $\pi\,:\, A\rightarrow q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes B)q$ such that $\pi(A)\subset q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes B)q$ is with expectation and $(1\otimes a)w=w\pi(a)$ for all $a\in A$.
    \end{enumerate}
If $A$ is finite $(1)$ and $(2)$ are also equivalent to:
\begin{enumerate}\setcounter{enumi}{2}
    \item There is no net of unitaries $(w_n)_n$ in $\mathcal{U}(A)$ such that $E_B(x^*w_ny)\rightarrow 0$ in the $\sigma$-strong topology, for all $x,y\in 1_AM1_B$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, for any $A$ (not necessarily finite or type ${\rm III}$), we have $(2)\Rightarrow (3)$.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- remark-22: body_md -->
\label{RmkNprec}
Let $A\subset 1_AM1_A$ and $B\subset 1_BM1_B$ with expectations and $\varphi$ a f.n.s. on $A$. If there exists a net of unitaries $(w_n)_n$ in $\mathcal{U}(A^\varphi)$ such that $E_B(x^*w_ny)\rightarrow 0$ in the $\sigma$-strong topology, for all $x,y\in 1_AM1_B$ then, $A\nprec_M B$. Indeed, by Proposition \ref{HI17thm} applied to the finite von Neumann algebra $A^\varphi$, we deduce that $A^\varphi\nprec_M B$. Note that $A^\varphi\subset A$ is unital and with expectation (by Takesaki's Theorem). Hence, Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(4)$ implies that $A\nprec_M B$.
<!-- end remark-22 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{diffusefd}
Let $M$ be a von Neumann algebra and $(u_n)_n$ a sequence in $M$ going to $0$ $\sigma$-weakly. Then, for any finite dimensional subalgebra $N\subset M$ and any normal conditional expectation $E\,:\, M\rightarrow N$, $ E(xu_n y) \rightarrow 0$ in the operator norm topology, for any $x,y\in M$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Let $\varphi\in N_*$ be a faithful state and fix an orthonormal basis $(e_i)_i$ of $N$ for the $\varphi$ scalar product. Then, $E(a) = \sum_{i} \varphi(e_i^* E(a))e_i=\sum_{i} \varphi\circ E(e_i^* a)e_i$. For all $x,y\in M$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \Vert E(xu_ny)\Vert &=& \left\Vert \sum_{i} \varphi\circ E(e_i^* xu_ny)e_i\right\Vert
 \leq  \sum_{i} \vert  \varphi\circ E(e_i^* xu_ny)\vert\cdot\Vert e_i\Vert,
\end{eqnarray*}
and this goes to $0$, because $u_n$ goes to $0$ weakly and the sum is finite. The same holds for the conjugate, because $a\mapsto a^*$ is weakly continuous. It concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- remark-23: body_md -->
\label{RmkDiffuse}
The previous Lemma applies in particular when $M$ is diffuse, $\varphi$ is almost periodic. In that case $M^\varphi$ is diffuse and the Lemma shows that there exists a sequence of unitaries $(u_n)_n$ in $M^\varphi$ such that, for any finite dimensional subalgebra $N$ of $M$ and any normal conditional expectation $E\,:\, M\rightarrow N$, $E(xu_ny)\rightarrow 0$ in norm.
<!-- end remark-23 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
{\cite[Lemma 2.6]{HU16b} \cite[Lemma 2.7]{HU16a}}\label{LemmaNets}
Let $M=(M_1,E_1)\ast_N (M_2,E_2)$ be an amalgamated free product and $\psi\in M_*$ a f.n.s. such that $\psi\circ E_{M_k}=\psi$ for $k=1,2$. If $(w_n)_n$ is a net in the unit ball of $(M_1)^\psi$ such that $E_1(xw_ny)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in M_1$ then,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $E_{M_1}(xw_ny)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in M\ominus M_1$.
    \item $E_{M_2}(xw_ny)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in M$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{LemmaNormalizer}
Let $M=M_1\ast_N M_2$ with $N$ is finite dimensional. Let $Q\subset M$ be any finite or type ${\rm III}$ diffuse von Neumann subalgebra with expectation. If $Q\prec_M M_1$ then $\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''\prec_M M_1$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Let $n\geq 1$, a projection $q\in M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1$, a non-zero partial isometry $w\in (M_{1,n}(\mathbb{C})\otimes M)q$ and a unital normal $*$-homomorphism $\pi\,:\, Q\rightarrow q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)q$ such that $\pi(Q)\subset q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)q$ is with expectation and $xw=w\pi(x)$ for all $x\in Q$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textbf{Claim:} \textit{One has $w^*w\in qM_n( M_1)q$ and $w^*\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''w\subset w^*wM_n(M_1)w^*w$.}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{Proof of the Claim.} We work in the amalgamated free product:
$$M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M=M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1\underset{M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes N}{*}M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_2,$$
with respect to the conditional expectation $\widetilde{E}_k:={\rm id}_{M_{n}(\mathbb{C})}\otimes E_k$, $k=1,2$.
Since $\pi(Q)$ is diffuse we may apply \cite[Lemma 2.1]{HU16b} to get a f.n.s. $\varphi$ on $\pi(Q)$ with diffuse centralizer $\pi(Q)^\varphi$ and note that $q=\pi(1)\in\pi(Q)^\varphi$. Define the normal state $\psi_1:=\varphi\circ E(q\,\cdot\,q)\in (M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)_*$, where $E\,:\, q (M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)q\rightarrow Q$ is any faithful normal conditional expectation. Fix any f.n.s. $\omega\in [(1-q)M(1-q)]_*$ and define the f.n.s. $\psi_2:=\frac{1}{2}\psi_1(\cdot)+\frac{1}{2}\omega((1-q)\cdot(1-q))\in (M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)_*$. Then, the f.n.s. $\psi:=\psi_2\circ({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})\in (M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M)_*$ satisfies the following: $\psi=\psi\circ({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})$, $q\in (M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)^\psi$ and $\pi(Q)\cap q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)^\psi q$ is diffuse. By Lemma \ref{diffusefd} there is a sequence of unitaries $(u_k)_k\in \pi(Q)\cap q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)^\psi q$ such that $\widetilde{E}_1(xu_ky)\rightarrow 0$ in norm, for all $x,y\in q(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)q$. Viewing the sequence $(u_k)_k$ in the unit ball of $(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)^\psi$ we can apply Lemma \ref{LemmaNets} and deduce that $({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(xu_ky)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly, for all $x,y\in q(M_n(M)\ominus M_n(M_1))q$. Fix a normalizing unitary $x\in\mathcal{N}_M(Q)$ and observe that, for all $a\in Q$, one has $w^*xw\pi(a)=w^*xaw=\pi(xax^*)w^*xw$. Define the element $v:=w^*xw-({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(w^*xw)\in qM_n(M)q$ and note that $({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(v)=0$. Moreover, for all $a\in Q$, one has $v\pi(a)=\pi(xax^*)v$. For any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, fix a unitary $a_k\in Q$ such that $\pi(a_k)=u_k$. Then, for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$, since $\pi(xa_kx^*)$ is a unitary in $\pi(Q)$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\Vert({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(vv^*)\Vert_\psi&=&\Vert\pi(xa_kx^*)({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(vv^*)\Vert_\psi
=\Vert({\rm id}\otimes E_{M_1})(vu_kv^*)\Vert_\psi\rightarrow_k0.
\end{eqnarray*}
It follows that $vv^*=0$ so $w^*xw\in M_n(M_1)$ for all $x\in \mathcal{N}_M(Q)$. This proves the Claim.\hfill\qedsymbol

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{End of the proof of Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer}.} By Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(2)$, it suffices to show that $$M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''\prec_{M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M} M_{n}(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1.$$
Since $xw=w\pi(x)$ for all $x\in Q$, we deduce that $ww^*\in Q'\cap M\subset\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''$. Define the projections $e:=e_{11}\otimes ww^*\in M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''$, $f:=w^*w\in M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1$ and note that, since $w$ is a partial isometry we have, viewing $w\in (e_{11}\otimes 1)(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M)$, $$ew=(e_{11}\otimes ww^*)w=ww^*w=w\text{ and }wf=ww^*w=w$$
so $w\in e(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M)f$. By the Claim, we have a unital normal $*$-homomorphism $$\theta\,:\,e(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathcal{N}_N(Q)'')e=\mathbb{C} e_{11}\otimes ww^*\mathcal{N}_N(Q)''ww^*\rightarrow w^*w(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)w^*w$$
defined by $\theta(e_{11}\otimes x)=w^*xw$ for all $x\in ww^*\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''ww^*$. Moreover, $w\theta(x)=ww^*xw=xw$ for all $x\in ww^*\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''ww^*$. Finally, note that the image of $\theta$ is exactly $w^*\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''w$ and, given any faithful normal conditional expectation $E\,:\, M\rightarrow\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''$, the map $$\widetilde{E}\,:\,w^*w(M_n(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_1)w^*w\rightarrow w^*\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''w,\quad\widetilde{E}(x):=w^*E(wxw^*)w$$
is obviously a normal faithful conditional expectation.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
{Special case of \cite[Theorem 5.2]{HI20}}\label{LemmaNormalizer1} Let $M=M_1\underset{N}{*}M_2$ and $Q\subset M_1$ a unital subalgebra with expectation. If $Q\nprec_{M_1}N$ then $\mathcal{N}_M(Q)''\subset M_1$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Since $Q\subset M_1$ is unital with expectation and $Q\nprec_{M_1}N$ we deduce from Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(2)$ that $M_1\nprec_{M_1} N$ so that we can directly apply \cite[Theorem 5.2]{HI20}.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{normalizerfp}
Let $M= M_1\underset{N}{*}M_2$ with $N$ finite dimensional. Then, for any finite diffuse and amenable subalgebra $A\subset M$ with expectation, one of the following statements holds:
\begin{itemize}
    \item There is a $k\in\{1,2\}$ such that $\mathcal{N}_M(A)''\prec_M M_k$,
    \item $\mathcal{N}_M(A)''$ is amenable.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Assume that $P:=\mathcal{N}_M(A)''\nprec_MM_k$ for $k=1,2$ and let us show that $P$ is amenable. By Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer} we have $A\nprec M_k$ for $k=1,2$. Hence, we may apply \cite[Theorem 4.4]{HU16a} and deduce that $A'\cap M$ is amenable. Let $\mathcal{A}:=A\vee(A'\cap M)\subset M$ and note that $\mathcal{A}$ is amenable and diffuse. Also, by Remark \ref{RmkExp}, $\mathcal{A}\subset M$ is with expectation. Define $\mathcal{P}:=\mathcal{N}_M(\mathcal{A})''$ and note that $P\subset\mathcal{P}$. By Remark \ref{RmkExp} $P\subset M$ is with expectation so $P\subset\mathcal{P}$ is with expectation and it suffices to show that $\mathcal{P}$ is amenable. Note that $\mathcal{A}'\cap M\subset A\subset \mathcal{A}$ and since $\mathcal{A}$ is diffuse and $N$ is finite dimensional, $\mathcal{A}\nprec_M N$. Also, since the inclusion $P\subset\mathcal{P}$ is unital with expectation, Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(2)$ implies that $\mathcal{P}\nprec_M M_k$ for $k=1,2$. Note that the statement of \cite[Theorem G]{IS22} is still valid, using normalizers instead of stable normalizers (and the proof is even easier, by using \cite[Theorem A.4]{HU16a} instead of \cite[Lemma 6.1]{IS22}). Hence, we deduce that $\mathcal{P}$ is amenable.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{HI20}
Let $M=\underset{N,1\leq i\leq K}{*}M_i$ be an amalgamated free product. Suppose that there exists $1\leq i\neq j\leq K$ such that $M_i\nprec_{M_i}N$ and the inclusion $N\subset M_j$ is entirely non trivial. Then, the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{Z}(M)=M'\cap N$.
\item For all f.n.s. $\varphi\in M_*$ such that $\varphi=\varphi\circ E_N$, we have
$$T(M):=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(N)\text{ such that }\sigma_t^\varphi={\rm Ad}(u)\}.$$
\item $M$ is semifinite if and only if there exists a faithful normal trace ${\rm Tr}_N$ on $N$ such that, for all $1\leq k\leq K$, ${\rm Tr}\circ E_k$ is a trace on $M_k$.
\item For every non-zero projection $z\in\mathcal{Z}(M)$, $Mz$ is not amenable relative to $M_i$ inside $M$. In particular, $Mz$ is not amenable.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
We write $M=M_i\underset{N}{*}M_i'$. Let us show that the inclusion $N\subset M_i'$ is entirely non trivial. If there is a non-zero projection $z\in\mathcal{Z}(N)$ such that $M_i'z=Nz$ then $M_jz\subset M_i'z=Nz$ which implies that $M_jz=Nz$. Since $N\subset M_j$ is entirely non-trivial, we deduce that $N\subset M_i'$ also is. Hence, we may apply \cite[Theorem A]{HI20} to deduce $(1)$, $(2)$ and $(4)$. It remains to show $(3)$ for which we can repeat the proof of \cite[Theorem 4.3 (3)]{Ue13}: fix any faithful normal state $\omega\in N_*$ and consider the state $\varphi:=\omega\circ E_N$. Then, $M$ is semifinite if and only if there exists one-parameter group of unitaries $u_t\in M$ such that $\sigma_t^\varphi={\rm Ad}(u_t)$ for all $t\in \mathbb{R}$. Fix $i$ such that $M_i\nprec_{M_i} N$. Applying Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer1} we deduce that $u_t\in M_i$, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Let now $j\neq i$ be such that $N\subset M_j$ is entirely non-trivial. Let $y\in M_j$ such that $E_j(y)=0$ and note that $\sigma_t^\varphi(y)(u_t-E_i(u_t))+ \sigma_t^\varphi(y)E_i(u_t)=\sigma_t^\varphi(y)u_t=u_ty=E_i(u_t)y+(u_t-E_i(u_t))y$. Writing $v:=u_t-E_i(u_t)$ we have, by freeness of $M_i$ and $M_j$ and since $\sigma_t^\varphi(y)\in\ker(E_j)$ and $v\in\ker(E_i)$,
$$
E_N(vyy^*v^*)=E_N(\sigma_t^\varphi(y)vy^*v^*)+E_N(\sigma_t^\varphi(y)E_i(u_t)y^*v^*)-E_i(u_t)E_N(yy^*v^*)=0.
$$
It follows that $E_N(vyy^*v^*)=E_N(vE_j(yy^*)v^*)=0$ and since $E_N$ is faithful, $vE_j(yy^*)=0$, for all $y\in\ker(E_j)$. Hence, $vs(E_j(yy^*))=0$, for all $y\in\ker(E_j)$, where $s(z)$ denotes the support projection of the self-adjoint operator $z$. By \cite[Lemma 4.2 (3)]{Ue13}, there is a family $(y_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements in $\ker(E_j)$ such that $\sum_{i\in i}s(E_j(y_iy_i^*))=1$. It implies that $v=0$ i.e. $u_t=E_i(u_t)\in N$. Write $u_t=h^{it}$ with $h$ a positive non-singular operator affiliated with the centralizer $N^\omega\subset N$ of $\sigma_t^\omega$. Then, the semifinite faithful normal weight $\omega_{h^{-1}}$ on $N$ is the desired trace.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{LemmaNprec}
Suppose that ${\rm Irr}(G)$ is infinite and ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite then, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, and all projection $q\in{\rm L}^\infty(G)'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ one has: $$L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})(1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes q)\nprec_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})(1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes q)}{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q.$$
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Since ${\rm Irr}(G)$ is infinite, it follows from \cite[Lemma 2.4]{FT24} that ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is diffuse. Hence, ${\rm L}^\infty(G)q$ is also diffuse. Moreover, since ${\rm L}^\infty(F)q\subset{\rm L}^\infty(G)q$ is a finite dimensional subalgebra and $h_G':=h_G(q)^{-1}h_G\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}$ is an almost periodic state on ${\rm L}^\infty(G)q$ (note that $q$ is in the centralizer of $h_G$), Remark \ref{RmkDiffuse} implies that there exists a sequence of unitaries $(u_n)_n$ in $({\rm L}^\infty(G)q)^{h'_G}$ such that $E_F(xu_ny)\rightarrow 0$ in norm, for all $x,y\in{\rm L}^\infty(G)q$. Considering the amalgamated free product:
\begin{eqnarray*}
    M&:=&(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))(1\otimes q)\simeq (B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q)\underset{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)\\
    &=:&M_1\underset{N}{*}M_2,
\end{eqnarray*}
Lemma \ref{LemmaNets} $(2)$ implies that $E_{M_2}(x(1\otimes u_n)y)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strong for all $x,y\in M$. We conclude from Remark \ref{RmkNprec} that $M\nprec_{M}M_2$. Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(3)$ implies that
\begin{equation*}
L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})(1\otimes q)\nprec_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})(1\otimes q)}{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q.\qedhere
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{LemmaVNBlock}
Suppose that $\beta$ is $2$-ergodic, ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Irr}(H)$ are infinite and ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite. For any $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ such that $N_\kappa\geq 2$ one has:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ is has no amenable direct summand and:
$$\mathcal{Z}( L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))=\mathbb{C}1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)).$$
\item For all non-zero projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$ one has:
$$T(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p)=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)\}\cap\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}\},$$
where $q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is the unique projection such that $p=1\otimes q$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
$(1)$. It suffices to prove the statement for $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_{\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$ instead of $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$. Since ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Irr}(H)$ are infinite, it follows from \cite[Lemma 2.4]{FT24} that both ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ and ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ are diffuse. Hence, since $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is finite dimensional, $$M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\nprec_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}\beta_\kappa(B)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$$
and, $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\subset B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is entirely non-trivial.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent From the discussion above, Theorem \ref{HI20} $(1)$ and Lemma \ref{LemmaT} $(2)$ we find that $$\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})))\subseteq\{u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)))\,:\,{\rm Ad}((\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(u))={\rm id}\}\subset\mathbb{C}1\otimes\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)).$$
Let $u\in\mathcal{Z}(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))$ and write $u=1\otimes v$, with $v\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$. Then, for all $x\in{\rm L}^\infty(G)$, $u(1_B\otimes x)u^*=1_B\otimes vxv^*=1_B\otimes x$, which implies that $v\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. The converse inclusion being trivial, this gives the formula for the center. Note that $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ has no amenable direct summand by Theorem \ref{HI20} $(4)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. Let $p\in\mathcal{Z}(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$ be a non-zero projection. Write $p=1\otimes q$ with $q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. Note that:
$$L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)=M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p=(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q)\underset{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}{*}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q).$$
Since ${\rm L}^\infty(G)q$ and ${\rm L}^\infty(H)$ are diffuse and $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$ is finite dimensional, we can apply Theorem \ref{HI20} $(2)$ and we find:
$$T(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p)=T(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p))=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists v\in\mathcal{U}(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)\,:\,\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)}={\rm Ad}(v)\},$$
Fix $t\in T(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p))$ and let $v\in\mathcal{U}(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ be such that $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)}={\rm Ad}(v)$. Note that, since $F$ is a finite quantum group, the Haar state of $F$ is tracial by \cite[Theorem 2.2]{VD97} so $\sigma_t^{h_F}={\rm id}$ hence, restricting the modular group of $\varphi_\kappa$ to $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, we find that $\sigma^{\psi_\kappa}_{-t}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_H}\otimes{\rm id}_{{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}={\rm Ad}((\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(v))$. Lemma \ref{LemmaT} implies that $v=1\otimes u$ for some unitary $u\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ and $\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}$. In particular, $\sigma_t^\psi={\rm id}$ and, restricting this time the modular group of $\varphi_\kappa$ to  $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q$ gives $\sigma_t^\psi\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm id}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(1\otimes u)$. Hence, $T(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p))\subseteq T'$, where:
$$T':=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)\}\cap\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}\}.$$
Let now $t\in T'$. Then $\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}$ implies that $\sigma_t^\psi={\rm id}_B$ and $\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}={\rm id}_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})}$. Let $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))$ be such that $\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)$. Then, $$\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}=\sigma_t^\psi\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(1\otimes u)\text{ and,}$$
$$\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}=\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_H}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_F}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}={\rm id}={\rm Ad}((\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes u))$$
since $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))$. It follows that $t\in T(L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p))$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{ThmFactor}
Suppose that $\beta$ be is a $2$-ergodic action, ${\rm dim}(B)\geq 3$, ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Irr}(H)$ are infinite and ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite. The following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ has no amenable direct summand and:
    $$\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))=
        \mathbb{C}1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes\left( {\rm L}^\infty(F)\cap\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\right).$$
        \item For all non-zero projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$ one has:
$$T({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p)=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)\}\cap\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}\},$$
where $q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is the unique projection such that $p=1\otimes q$.
    \item For all non-zero projection  $p\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$ the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item $H$ is Kac and there exists a positive and invertible element $Q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ 
    such that $\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(Q^{it})$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$, where $q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is the unique projection such that $p=1\otimes q$.
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ is finite.
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ is semifinite.
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
We write ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=\underset{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F),1\leq\gamma\leq K}{*}L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$ and since $L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})}{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ (Lemma \ref{LemmaNprec}) we have in particular that the inclusion ${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\subset L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$ is entirely non-trivial, for $1\leq\gamma\leq K$.
\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(1)$. Note that we always have $\mathbb{C}1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes ({\rm L}^\infty(F)\cap\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G)))\subseteq\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$. If $K=1$ statement $(1)$ follows directly from Lemma \ref{LemmaVNBlock} (since ${\rm dim}(B)\geq 3$). Hence we may and will assume that $K\geq 2$ so that we can apply Theorem \ref{HI20} to deduce that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ has no amenable direct summand. Let $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})))$. If there exists $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ such that $N_\kappa\geq 2$ then, since $u\in \mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$, it follows from Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer1} that $u$ is in the center of $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$. We deduce that $u\in\mathbb{C}1_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)}\otimes ({\rm L}^\infty(F)\cap\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G)))$ by Lemma \ref{LemmaVNBlock}. Hence, we may and will assume that $N_\kappa=1$ for all $\kappa$. Hence, $B=\mathbb{C}^K$ and $K\geq 3$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Let $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})))$. By Theorem \ref{HI20}, $u\in{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. In particular, $u\in\mathcal{Z}(L_1(\mathbb{G}))\cap\mathcal{Z}(L_2(\mathbb{G}))$. For each $1\leq\kappa\leq K$, we can again apply Theorem \ref{HI20} to the amalgamated free product $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})=(\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))\underset{\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}{*}({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))$ to deduce:
$$\mathcal{Z}(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))\subseteq\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))\cap\beta_\kappa(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F).$$
In particular, $u\in(\beta_1(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))\cap(\beta_2(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))=\mathbb{C}1\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$, by Lemma \ref{LemmaTdim1}. Then, there exists $v\in{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ such that $u=1\otimes v$ and since $u$ is central in $\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)$, we have $v\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))$. Hence, $\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))\subseteq \mathbb{C}1\otimes\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. Once again, we may and will assume that $K\geq 2$, By Lemma \ref{LemmaVNBlock}. Let $p=1\otimes q$ be a projection in $\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$, with $q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. Note that $p$ is in the centralizer of $h_{\mathbb{G}}$ and $q$ is in the centralizer of $h_G$ and:
$${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p\simeq\underset{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q,1\leq\gamma\leq K}{*}L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p.$$
Since $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p\nprec_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p}{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$ (Lemma \ref{LemmaNprec}) we have $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}( L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p)\subset L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p$ for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$, by Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer1}. Define:
$$T':=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)\}\cap\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}\}.$$
Let $t\in T'$ and let $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q))$ such that $\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(u)$. Since $\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}$ one has $\sigma_t^\psi={\rm id}$ and $\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\gamma}={\rm id}$ for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$. Arguing as in the end of the proof of Lemma \ref{LemmaVNBlock}, we deduce that $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\gamma}\vert_{L(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\gamma)(1\otimes p)}={\rm Ad}(v)$, where
$$v:=(1\otimes u)=(\beta_\gamma\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes u)\in\mathcal{U}(L_\gamma(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p))\subset\mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)),\text{ for all }\gamma\in\{1,\dots,K\}.$$ Hence $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\gamma}\vert_{L(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\gamma)(1\otimes p)}$ is actually implemented by the same unitary in ${\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$. Since the isomorphism $M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p\simeq L_\gamma(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)$ intertwines $\psi_\gamma^{-1}\otimes h_\gamma\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}$, it intertwines the modular automorphisms $\sigma_t^{\psi_\gamma^{-1}}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}={\rm id}_{M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}$ and $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)}$ and since the isomorphism is the inclusion on ${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, ${\rm id}_{M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}$ and hence $\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}$ is implemented by the same unitary in ${\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$. Since $\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}=\underset{1\leq \gamma\leq K}{*}\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}\vert_{L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p}$, we deduce that $t\in T({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Let us prove the converse inclusion. Let $t\in T({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p)$. Then, there exists $v\in\mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p)$ such that $\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}={\rm Ad}(v)$. Since $\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}({L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})})=\sigma_t^{h_\gamma}(L_\gamma(\mathbb{G}))=L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$, we have $v\in\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}(L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p)\subset L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p$, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$. If there exists $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ such that $N_\kappa\geq 2$ then it follows that $t\in T(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p)$ so $t\in T'$, by Lemma \ref{LemmaVNBlock}. Hence, we may and will assume that $N_\kappa=1$, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$. In that case, $B=\mathbb{C}^K$, $K\geq 3$ and $\psi$ is the uniform trace since it is the unique $\delta$-form on $\mathbb{C}^K$. Viewing, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$,
$$L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p=(\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q)\underset{\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}{*}({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$$
and observing that:
$${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}\beta_\kappa(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q\text{ and,}$$
$$\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q\nprec_{\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F),$$
we may apply Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer1} to deduce that $v\in (\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q)\cap({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)\subset L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})q$, for all $1\leq \gamma\leq K$. In particular, $v\in\beta_1(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q\cap\beta_2(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q=\mathbb{C}1\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, by Lemma \ref{LemmaTdim1}. Write $v=1\otimes u$, where $u\in\mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$. Since, $\sigma_t^\psi\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}={\rm id}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}={\rm Ad}(1\otimes u)$ we deduce that $\sigma_t^{h_G}={\rm Ad}(u)$ and $u\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$ (since $F$ is Kac). We also have $\sigma_t^{h_H}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_F}={\rm Ad}((\beta_1\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes u))={\rm id}$, which implies that $\sigma_t^{h_H}={\rm id}$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(3)$. We fix a projection $p\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$ and we write $p=1\otimes q$, where $q\in \mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is a projection. 
\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(a)\Rightarrow(b)$. Assume that $H$ is Kac and there exists $Q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ positive and invertible such that $\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(Q^{it})$. Then $\psi$ and $\psi_\kappa^{-1}$ are traces so $$\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}={\rm id}={\rm Ad}((\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes Q^{it}))$$
since $Q\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$. Also, $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm id}\otimes\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(1\otimes Q^{it})$. Hence, $\sigma_t^{\varphi_\kappa}\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p}={\rm Ad}(Q_1^{it})$, where $Q_1:=(1\otimes Q)=(\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes Q)\in L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})p$, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$. Arguing as in the end of the proof of $(2)$, we deduce that $\sigma_t^{h_\kappa}\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})p}$ is implemented by the same unitary $Q_1^{it}\in{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ and  so $\sigma_t^{h_\mathbb{G}}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}$ is also implemented by $Q_1^{it}\in{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. It follows that the faithful state $\tau=h_{\mathbb{G}}(p)^{-1}h_\mathbb{G}(Q_1^{-1}\cdot)\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p}$ is a trace on ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$.

\vspace{0.2cm}\noindent$(b)\Rightarrow(c)$ is obvious.


\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(c)\Rightarrow(a)$. Assume that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ is semifinite. Hence, $T({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p)=\mathbb{R}$ and it follows from $(2)$ that $H$ is Kac. In particular, $\psi$ is a tracial $\delta$-form so it is the uniform trace on $B$ i.e. $\psi=\frac{1}{K}\sum_\kappa\frac{1}{N_\kappa}{\rm Tr}_\kappa$ (and $\psi_\gamma$ is tracial, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$). Moreover, since $L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})p$ has expectation, $L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p$ is semifinite, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$, so $L_\gamma(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)=M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})p$ also is. Write $L_\gamma(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})(1\otimes p)=(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q)\underset{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q}{*}(M_{N_\gamma}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ and apply Theorem \ref{HI20} $(3)$ to deduce that there exists a faithful normal semifinite trace $\omega$ on $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$ such that $\omega\circ({\rm id}\otimes E_F)$ is tracial on $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)q$. Note that, since  $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$ is finite dimensional, $\omega$ is actually finite and up to renormalization, we may and will assume that $\omega$ is a faithful normal tracial state on $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q$. Then, there exists $Q_0\in\mathcal{Z}(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ positive and invertible such that $\omega=(\psi\otimes h_{F})(Q_0\cdot)$. Write $Q_0=\sum_{\gamma,r}e^\gamma_{rr}\otimes Q_\gamma$, where $Q_\gamma\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ is positive and invertible. In particular, $Q:=\frac{1}{K}\sum_\gamma Q_\gamma\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)q)$ is positive and invertible and, for all $x\in {\rm L}^\infty(G)q$, one has:
\begin{eqnarray*}
\omega\circ({\rm id}\otimes E_F)(1\otimes x)&=&\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\gamma,r}\frac{1}{N_\gamma}({\rm Tr}_\gamma\otimes h_F)(e^\gamma_{rr}\otimes Q_\gamma E_F(x))=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\gamma}h_F(Q_\gamma E_F(x))\\
&=&\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\gamma}h_F( E_F(Q_\gamma x))=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{\gamma}h_G(Q_\gamma x)=h_G(Qx).
\end{eqnarray*}
Note that the modular group of $h_G(Q\cdot)\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}$ is given by $Q^{it}\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}(\cdot)Q^{-it}$. Since $\omega\circ({\rm id}\otimes E_F)$ is tracial, the faithful state $h_G(Q\cdot)\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}$ also is hence $Q^{it}\sigma_t^{h_G}(\cdot)\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}Q^{-it}={\rm id}$ and $\sigma_t^{h_G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(G)q}={\rm Ad}(Q^{-it})$, for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- remark-24: body_md -->
Note that condition $(a)$ in statement $(3)$ of the previous Theorem implies in particular that ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is a finite von Neumann algebra.
<!-- end remark-24 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{ThmFactor}, ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is a factor when the amalgam $F$ is trivial. However, coming back to the example $\mathbb{G}:=\widehat{\Gamma}\wr_{*,\beta}\widehat{\Lambda}$ given in Section \ref{SectionNewExample}, Remark \ref{RemarkNewExample} implies that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=L(\Gamma)^{*\vert\Lambda\vert}\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(\Lambda)$ whenever $\Lambda$ is abelian. Hence, ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is never a factor, as soon as $\Lambda$ is a non-trivial abelian finite group.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
If $\beta$ is $2$-ergodic, ${\dim}(B)\geq 3$, both ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Irr}(H)$ are infinite and ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite then $ T^\tau_{\rm Int}(\mathbb{G}) = \{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))\,\,\tau_t^G={\rm Ad}(u)\} \cap T^\tau(H)$.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Let $t\in T^\tau_{\rm Int}(\mathbb{G})$ and $u_0\in \mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))$ such that $\tau^\mathbb{G}_{t} = {\rm Ad}(u_0)$. Since $\tau^\mathbb{G}_t$ preserves the subalgebras $L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, and $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}(L_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))''\subset L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ we deduce that $u_0\in L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent First assume that, for some $1\le\kappa\leq K$, $N_\kappa\geq 2$. Identifying $L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ with $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})$ and $\widetilde{\tau}^\kappa_t:=\tau_t^{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}\vert_{L_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}$ with $\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\tau_t^{\mathbb{G}}\vert_{L_\kappa(\mathbb{G})}$ we can write $\widetilde{\tau}^\kappa_t={\rm Ad}(w)$, where $w=v\otimes u_0$ for some $v\in\mathcal{U}(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C}))$. Viewing ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ as an amalgamated free product and since, by construction, $\widetilde{\tau}^\kappa_t$ leaves globally invariant both subalgebras $B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)$ and $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ we deduce that there exists $u$ in the amalgam $M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ such that $\widetilde{\tau}^\kappa_t={\rm Ad}(u)$. In particular, $\sigma_{-t}^{\psi_\kappa}\otimes\tau_t^H\otimes{\rm id}={\rm Ad}((\beta_\kappa\otimes{\rm id})(u))$ (since $\tau_t^F$ is trivial, because ${\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is finite dimensional). Lemma \ref{LemmaT} gives that $u\in \mathbb{C}1\otimes \mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$ and $\tau_t^H={\rm id}$. Hence, viewing $u\in \mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$ we have $\tau_t^G={\rm Ad}(u)$.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Now assume that $N_\kappa=1$, for all $1\leq\kappa\leq K$ so that $B=\mathbb{C}^K$, ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})={\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, $K\geq 3$ and $\psi$ is the uniform trace since it is the unique $\delta$-form on $\mathbb{C}^K$. Viewing, for all $1\leq\gamma\leq K$,
$$L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})=(\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))\underset{\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}{*}({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))$$
 and since $\tau_t^\mathbb{G}$ leaves globally invariant both $\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G)$ and ${\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$, we may apply Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer1} to deduce that $u_0\in (\mathbb{C}^K\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))\cap({\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F))\subset L_\gamma(\mathbb{G})$, for all $1\leq \gamma\leq K$. In particular, $u_0\in\beta_1(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)\cap\beta_2(\mathbb{C}^K)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)=\mathbb{C}1\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$, by Lemma \ref{LemmaTdim1}. Write $u_0=1\otimes u$, where $u\in\mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$. Since $$\tau_t^\mathbb{G}\vert_{\mathbb{C}^K\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(G)}=\sigma_{-t}^\psi\otimes\tau_t^{h_G}={\rm Ad}(1\otimes u)={\rm id}\otimes{\rm Ad}(u)$$ we deduce that $\tau_t^{h_G}={\rm Ad}(u)$ and $u\in\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F))$ (since ${\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is finite dimensional). We also have:
 $$\tau_t^\mathbb{G}\vert_{{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}=\tau_t^{H}\otimes\tau_t^{F}={\rm Ad}((\beta_1\otimes{\rm id})(1\otimes u))={\rm id},$$
 which implies that $\tau_t^{H}={\rm id}$. This shows the first inclusion.
 
 \vspace{0.2cm}
 
 \noindent Let now $t\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that $\tau_t^H={\rm id}$ and $u\in\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(F)))$ such that $\tau_t^G={\rm Ad}(u)$. By construction of $\tau_t^{\mathbb{G}}$, we can argue as the in proof of the $T$-invariant computation in Theorem \ref{ThmFactor} to deduce that $\tau_t^{\mathbb{G}}={\rm Ad}(u)$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- remark-25: body_md -->
Under the hypothesis of the previous Proposition and if $F$ is moreover trivial then $T^\tau_{\rm Int}(\mathbb{G})=T^\tau(G)\cap T^\tau(H)=T^\tau(\mathbb{G})$. In particular, the Vaes $T$-invariant \cite{Va05}
$$T_V(\mathbb{G}):=\{t\in\mathbb{R}\,:\,\exists u\in\mathcal{U}({\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}))\,\,\tau_t^\mathbb{G}={\rm Ad}(u)\text{ and }\Delta_\mathbb{G}(u)=u\otimes u\}$$ satisfies
$T_V(\mathbb{G})=T^\tau_{\rm Int}(\mathbb{G})=T^\tau(\mathbb{G})=T^\tau(G)\cap T^\tau(H)$.
<!-- end remark-25 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{ThmPrimeCartan}
Suppose that $\beta$ be is a $2$-ergodic action, ${\rm dim}(B)\geq 3$, ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Irr}(H)$ are infinite,  ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite and ${\rm L}^\infty(F)\cap\mathcal{Z}({\rm L}^\infty(G))=\mathbb{C}1$. Then ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is a non-amenable factor of type ${\rm II}_1$ or ${\rm III}$ satisfying the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is prime.
    \item ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ does not have any Cartan subalgebra.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
The fact that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is a non-amenable factor of type ${\rm II}_1$ or ${\rm III}$ follows from Theorem \ref{ThmFactor}. Using the notations of Remark \ref{rmk fd amal}, we write ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ as an amalgamated free product: $$ {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}) \simeq M_K \simeq M_{K-1} \underset{B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(F)}{\ast} \nu_K(B\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(G)).$$ To simplify the notations we write $M$ for $M_{K-1}$. We then have the following Claim.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textbf{Claim.} \textit{One has ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})} M$ and ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})} \nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$.}

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{Proof of the Claim.} Since ${\rm Irr}(G)$ is infinite, the von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}^\infty(G)$ is diffuse \cite[Lemma 2.4]{FT24} and since the Haar state of $G$ is almost periodic, its centralizer ${\rm L}^\infty(G)^{h_G}$ is still diffuse. Let $(u_n)_n$ be a sequence of unitaries in ${\rm L}^\infty(G)^{h_G}$ going to $0$ $\sigma$-weakly. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})=\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))*_{B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)}M$ we may apply Lemma \ref{diffusefd} to deduce that $$({\rm id}_B\otimes E_F'')(x(1\otimes u_n)y)\rightarrow 0\,\, \text{ in norm for all }x,y\in B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G).$$
Since $\nu_K(1\otimes u_n)$ is in the centralizer of $h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}$ for all $n$, we may apply Lemma \ref{LemmaNets} to deduce that $E_{M}(x\nu_K(1\otimes u_n)y)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. In particular, $E_{M}(x\rho^K_{ij}(u_n)y)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ and $1\leq i,j\leq N_\kappa$. Note that the map $$\rho_K\,:\, {\rm L}^\infty(G)\rightarrow M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G}),\quad a\mapsto\sum_{i,j}e^K_{ij}\otimes\rho^K_{ij}(a)$$ is a unital $*$-homomorphism so that $\rho_K(u_n)$ is unitary in $M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$. Moreover,
$$E_{M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes M}(X\rho_K(u_n)Y)=\sum_{i,j,r,s}e^K_{ij}\otimes E_{M}(X_{ir}\rho^\kappa_{rs}(u_n)Y_{sj})\rightarrow 0\,\,\sigma\text{-strongly}$$
for all $X,Y\in M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Since $M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is finite or of type ${\rm III}$ we have $$M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes {\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})} M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes M.$$
Hence, ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M$.


\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent Now, since ${\rm Irr}(H)$ is infinite and arguing as in the beginning of the proof, we have a sequence of unitaries $(v_n)_n$ in ${\rm L}^\infty(H)^{h_H}$ going to $0$ $\sigma$-weakly so $1\otimes v_n\otimes 1\in M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$ is going to $0$ $\sigma$-weakly and, by Lemma \ref{diffusefd}, we deduce that $(E_K\otimes{\rm id}_F)(x(1\otimes v_n\otimes 1)y)\rightarrow 0$ in norm, for all $x,y\in M_{N_K}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(H)\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(F)$. Next, since $\mu(v_n\otimes 1)\in M$ is in the centralizer of $h_{\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}}$ for all $n$, we can apply Lemma \ref{LemmaNets} and deduce that $E_{\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))}(x\mu(v_n\otimes 1)y)\rightarrow 0$ $\sigma$-strongly for all $x,y\in{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Note that $\mu(v_n\otimes 1)$ is actually a sequence of unitaries in ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is finite or type ${\rm III}$, we deduce that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$.$\qed$

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent\textit{End of the proof of Theorem \ref{ThmPrimeCartan}.}$(1)$. By contradiction, assume that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=P\otimes Q$, where $P$ and $Q$ are two diffuse factors. Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is either finite or type ${\rm III}$ we may and will assume that both $P$ and $Q$ are either finite or of type ${\rm III}$. Moreover, since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is not amenable one of them, let say $P$, is not amenable. Note that, since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=P\otimes Q$, there is a normal faithful conditional expectation from ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ to $Q$ (and to $P$) and since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ has expectation, we deduce that both $Q, P\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ have expectation. Since $Q$ is diffuse, we may apply \cite[Lemma 2.1]{HU16b} to get a f.n.s. $\omega\in Q_*$ with diffuse centralizer $A:=Q^\omega\subset Q$. Note that $A\subset Q$ has expectation by Takesaki's Theorem hence $A\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ also has expectation. Also, $P\subset Q'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset A'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset A'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Since $P$ is not amenable and has expectation, $A'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is not amenable either. Since $A$ is finite, diffuse and has expectation we may apply \cite[Theorem 4.4]{HU16a} to deduce that either $A\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$ or $A\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M$. Applying now Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer} we deduce that $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$ or $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M$. Since $P\subset A'\cap{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$, Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(4)$ implies that $P\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$ or $P\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M$. Applying again Lemma \ref{LemmaNormalizer} we get that $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(P)''\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))$ or $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(P)''\prec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M$. However, $P,Q\subset\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(P)''$ which implies that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(P)''$ so that, with Remark \ref{RmkEmbedds} $(4)$ and the Claim, we obtain a contradiction.

\vspace{0.2cm}

\noindent$(2)$. By contradiction, let $A\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ be a Cartan subalgebra (with expectation). Since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ has expectation, $A\subset{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ has expectation. Note that ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})=\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})}(A)''\subset \mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''$. Hence, the Claim implies that
$$ \mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}\nu_K(B\otimes{\rm L}^\infty(G))\text{ and }\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''\nprec_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}M.$$
Moreover, since ${\rm L}^\infty(\mathbb{G})$ is not amenable and has expectation, $\mathcal{N}_{{\rm L}^\infty(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})}(A)''$ is not amenable either. We get a contradiction with Lemma \ref{normalizerfp}.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{1nontor}
For a compact quantum group $G$, the class of the unit $[1]\in K_0(C(G))$ is never $0$ or of torsion. If $G$ is K-amenable, then this is also true for $[1]\in K_0(C_r(G))$.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
We use the counit, which is a $*$-morphism $\varepsilon : C(G)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$, which gives $\varepsilon_\ast : K_0(C(G)) \rightarrow K_0(\mathbb{C})\simeq \mathbb{Z}$, sending $[1]$ to $[1]$, which is the generator of the K-theory group of $\mathbb{C}$. Therefore the class cannot be of torsion. If $G$ is K-amenable, the same holds for the reduced C*-algebra, because $\lambda_\ast$, which is an isomorphism in that case, sends the class $[1]$ to $[1]$ too.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{Morita}
For any element $\gamma = [H,\eta, F]\in KK(A,B)$, the Kasparov product of $m_A$ and $\gamma$ is given by $m_A\otimes\gamma=[\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H, {\rm id}\otimes \eta, 1\otimes F]\in KK(M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes A,B).$
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The Kasparov product of $m_A$ and $\gamma$ can be taken as $[(\mathbb{C}^N \otimes A)\otimes_A H, {\rm id} \otimes_\eta 1, \Tilde{F}]$, where $\Tilde{F}$ is an adequate $F$-connection making it a Kasparov triple. There is a unitary isomorphism 
\begin{align*}
U : (\mathbb{C}^N \otimes A)\otimes_A H&\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^N\otimes H \\
(f\otimes a) \otimes_\eta \xi &\mapsto f\otimes \eta(a)\xi.
\end{align*}
Under this isomorphism, the map ${\rm id}\otimes_\eta 1$ corresponds to the map $U({\rm id}\otimes_\eta 1)U^*$ which sends any element $b\otimes a\in M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes A$ to $b\otimes \eta(a)\in \mathcal{L}(\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H)$. We then fix $\Tilde{F}$ to be the operator $U (1\otimes F) U^*$, and we only have to check that $\Tilde{F}$ is a $F$-connection and that it defines a Kasparov module.
First, for any $b\otimes a\in M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes A$, we have 
$$[({\rm id}\otimes\eta)(b\otimes a), 1\otimes F] = b \otimes [\eta(a), F],$$
which is a compact operator because $[\eta(a), F]$ is, by hypothesis, and $\mathbb{C}^N$ is finite dimensional. The same way, $(1\otimes F)^2 ({\rm id}\otimes \eta)(b\otimes a) = b\otimes F^2\eta(a)$ and
$$(1\otimes F-1\otimes F^*)({\rm id}\otimes \eta)(b\otimes a) = b\otimes (F-F^*)\eta(a)$$
are also compact operators. Lastly, we have to check the connection properties. For any $x\in (\mathbb{C}^N \otimes A)$, we define the adjointable map $T_x \in \mathcal{L}(H, (\mathbb{C}^N \otimes A)\otimes_A H), \xi\mapsto x\otimes_\eta \xi$. Then if $x= f\otimes a$, the map $UT_x$ becomes $\xi \mapsto f \otimes \eta(a)\xi$ hence:
$$T_x F - \Tilde{F}T_x = T_xF-U^*(1\otimes F)UT_x= U^*(UT_xF-(1\otimes F)UT_x).$$
For any $\xi$, we have $(T_x F - \Tilde{F}T_x)\xi = U^*(f\otimes (\eta(a)F\xi-F\eta(a)\xi))$, which is a compact operator by hypothesis. The other property can be shown the same way. Thus this indeed defines a Kasparov product for $m_A\otimes \gamma$, which corresponds to $[\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H, {\rm id}\otimes \eta, 1\otimes F]$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thmDtxt}
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $G$ and $H$ are K-amenable.
    \item $\mathbb{G}$ is K-amenable.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
$(1)\Rightarrow (2)$.
Assume first that $G$ and $H$ are K-amenable, then we can apply \cite[Theorem 5.1]{FG18} to the amalgamated free product $$ C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\simeq (B\otimes C_\bullet(G))\underset{B\otimes C_\bullet(F)}{\ast_\bullet} (M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H\times F)),$$ to get that the full algebra $C_\kappa(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ is K-equivalent to the reduced $C_{r,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ for all $\kappa$, through the canonical map $\widetilde{\lambda_\kappa}$ and as $C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})\simeq M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})$, the same is true for the map $\lambda_\kappa$ such that $\widetilde{\lambda_\kappa}={\rm id} \otimes \lambda_\kappa$. We then apply it to $$ C_\bullet(\mathbb{G})\simeq \underset{C_\bullet(H\times F)}{\ast_\bullet} C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}),$$ to get that $\mathbb{G}$ is K-amenable.

\noindent$(2)\Rightarrow (1).$
Assume that $\mathbb{G}$ is K-amenable i.e. there exists $\gamma \in KK(C_r(\mathbb{G}),\mathbb{C})$ such that $[\lambda_\mathbb{G}] \otimes \gamma = [\varepsilon_\mathbb{G}]\in KK(C(\mathbb{G}),\mathbb{C})$. Then, since $H$ is a dual quantum subgroup of $\mathbb{G}$, it is also K-amenable. We then fix any $1\leq \kappa\leq K$, and we consider the morphism $\pi :C(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(\mathbb{G})$ defined by $\pi : a \mapsto \beta_\kappa(e^\kappa_{11})\rho_\kappa(a)$. Note that $({\rm id}\otimes \varepsilon_\mathbb{G})\circ \pi = \varepsilon_G(\cdot)e_{11}^\kappa$. By Theorem \ref{TheoremErgodic} we have $({\rm id}_B\otimes h_\mathbb{G})\rho=h_G(\cdot)1_B$. In particular, $({\rm id}\otimes h_\mathbb{G})\rho_\kappa=h_G(\cdot)1$. It follows that there exists a unique unital $*$-homomorphism $\rho_{r,\kappa}\,:\,C_r(G)\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_r(\mathbb{G})$ such that $({\rm id}\otimes\lambda_\mathbb{G})\rho_\kappa=\rho_{r,\kappa}\lambda_G$. Viewing $\beta_\kappa(e^\kappa_{11})$ as a projection in $ (M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes{\rm Pol}(H))\cap\rho_{r,\kappa}(C_r(G))'$, the map $\rho_{r,\kappa}(C_r(G))\rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_r(\mathbb{G})$, $x\mapsto\beta_\kappa(e^\kappa_{11})x$ is a (non-unital) $*$-homomorphism. Hence $\pi_r: C_r(G) \rightarrow M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_r(\mathbb{G})$ defined by $\pi_r(a):=\beta_\kappa(e^\kappa_{11})\rho_{r,\kappa}(a)$ is such that $\pi_r\circ \lambda_G = ({\rm id} \otimes \lambda_\mathbb{G})\circ \pi$. Let us show that $\Tilde{\gamma} := [\pi_r] \otimes m_{C_r(\mathbb{G})} \otimes \gamma \in KK(C_r(G),\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $[\lambda_G]\otimes \Tilde{\gamma} =[\varepsilon_G]$. Using Lemma \ref{Morita} we find:
\begin{align*}
    [\lambda_G] \otimes \Tilde{\gamma} &= [\lambda_G]\otimes [\pi_r] \otimes m_{C_r(\mathbb{G})} \otimes \gamma= [\pi_r\circ \lambda_G]\otimes m_{C_r(\mathbb{G})}\otimes\gamma\\
                   &= [({\rm id}\otimes\lambda_\mathbb{G})\circ \pi]\otimes [\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H, {\rm id}\otimes \eta, 1\otimes F]\\
                   &= [\pi]\otimes [{\rm id}\otimes \lambda_\mathbb{G}]\otimes [\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H, {\rm id}\otimes \eta, 1\otimes F]\\
                   &= [\pi]\otimes[\mathbb{C}^N\otimes H, ({\rm id}\otimes \eta\lambda_\mathbb{G}), 1\otimes F]
                   = [\pi]\otimes m_{C(\mathbb{G})}\otimes [H,  \eta\lambda_\mathbb{G}, F]\\
                   &= [\pi]\otimes m_{C(\mathbb{G})}\otimes [\lambda_\mathbb{G}]\otimes [H,  \eta, F]
                   = [\pi]\otimes m_{C(\mathbb{G})}\otimes [\lambda_\mathbb{G}]\otimes \gamma
                   = [\pi]\otimes m_{C(\mathbb{G})}\otimes [\varepsilon_\mathbb{G}]\\
                   &= [\pi] \otimes m_{C(\mathbb{G})}\otimes [\mathbb{C},\varepsilon_\mathbb{G},0]
                   = [\pi] \otimes [\mathbb{C}^N,{\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_\mathbb{G},0]
                   = [\mathbb{C}^N,({\rm id}\otimes\varepsilon_\mathbb{G})\circ \pi,0]\\
                   &= [\mathbb{C}^N,\varepsilon_G(\cdot)e_{11}^\kappa,0]= [\mathbb{C},\varepsilon_G,0]\oplus [\mathbb{C}^{N-1},0,0]=[\varepsilon_G],
\end{align*}
because the action of $e_{11}^\kappa$ is only on the first coordinate in $\mathbb{C}^{N}$, and the second summand is a degenerate module. Hence $[\lambda_G]\otimes \Tilde{\gamma} =[\varepsilon_G]$ and $G$ is K-amenable.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{exactseq1}
For a compact quantum group $G$ with a dual quantum subgroup $F$, and a compact quantum group $H$ acting on $(B,\psi)$, and there is an exact sequence of K-theory:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}[sep=small]
\scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_0(B\otimes C_\bullet(F)))}}} \arrow[r] & \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_0(B\otimes C_\bullet(G))}}} \oplus \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H\times F))}}} \arrow[r] & \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))}}} \arrow[d]\\
 \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))}}} \arrow[u] & \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_1(B\otimes C_\bullet(G)) \oplus K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H\times F))}}} \arrow[l] & \scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_1(B\otimes C_\bullet(F))}}}. \arrow[l]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
Moreover, the vertical arrow on the right is zero as soon as ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite, and the vertical arrow on the left is zero as soon as the map $\iota_\ast : K_0(C_\bullet(F))\rightarrow K_0(C_\bullet(G))$ is injective.
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
We write $$M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})\simeq (B\otimes C_\bullet(G))\underset{B\otimes C_\bullet(F)}{\ast_\bullet} (M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H\times F)),$$
and we can immediately apply the result of \cite{FG20} to get the exact sequences for the reduced and the full case. Now assume that ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite. Then $C(F)\simeq C_r(F)\simeq {\rm Pol}(F)$ is a finite dimensional C*-algebra, therefore we have immediately $K_1(B\otimes C_\bullet(F))=0$ and so the vertical map on the right-hand side is $0$. We can also deduce from this that $$K_0( M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H) \otimes C(F))\simeq K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H)) \otimes K_0(C(F)),$$ and we also have in any case $$K_0(B\otimes C_\bullet(F))\simeq K_0(B)\otimes K_0(C_\bullet(F)). $$ 
Using that $\iota_\ast : K_0(C_\bullet(F))\rightarrow K_0(C_\bullet(G))$ is injective, we see that the first horizontal map must be injective in the full case. This also implies that the left vertical map is $0$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- remark-26: body_md -->
In the case where $F$ is trivial and we consider the maximal C*-algebras, Proposition \ref{1nontor} shows that the map $\iota_\ast : \mathbb{C} \rightarrow K_0(C(G))$ is injective, so the vertical arrow on the left is zero. This is also true for the reduced C*-algebras is $G$ has a K-amenable dual.
<!-- end remark-26 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
If ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite and $\iota_*\,:\, K_0(C(F))\rightarrow K_0(C_\bullet(G))$ is injective then, we have an isomorphism $$ K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})) \simeq K_1(B\otimes C_\bullet(G)) \oplus K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H)\otimes C(F)), $$ and a short exact sequence $$\scalebox{0.88}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle 0\rightarrow K_0(B\otimes C(F)) \rightarrow K_0(B\otimes C_\bullet(G)) \oplus K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H)\otimes C(F))\rightarrow K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))\rightarrow 0.}}}$$
