This shows that the group $K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))$ is the quotient
$$\scalebox{0.85}{\mbox{\ensuremath{\displaystyle K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})) \simeq K_0(B\otimes C_{\bullet}(G)) \oplus K_0(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet}(H)\otimes C(F))/ <[e_{11}^\gamma\otimes f]-[\beta_\kappa(e_{11}^\gamma)\otimes f]>,}}}$$ where $f\in C(F)$ are projections corresponding to the generators of $K_0(C(F))$ and $1\leq \gamma\leq K$.
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
There is a 6-term exact sequence
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
\bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^{K-1}K_0(C_\bullet(H\times F)) \arrow[r] & \bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^K K_0(C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})) \arrow[r] & K_0(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G})) \arrow[d]\\
 K_1(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G})) \arrow[u] & \bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^K K_1(C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G})) \arrow[l] & \bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^{K-1}K_1(C_\bullet(H\times F)). \arrow[l]
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
Moreover, when ${\rm Irr}(F)$ is finite, the map on the right is $0$, and if $F$ is trivial, then the first map on the left is also $0$, in the maximal case.
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
The exact sequence is a direct application of \cite{FG20} to the amalgamated free product. 
The map $K_1(C_\bullet(H\times F)) \rightarrow K_1(C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))$ corresponds to $\iota_\ast$, while the map in the part of the isomorphism $K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_\bullet(H\times F)) \hookrightarrow K_1(M_{N_\kappa}(\mathbb{C})\otimes C_{\bullet,\kappa}(\mathbb{G}))$ corresponds to $({\rm id}\otimes \iota)_\ast$, which is injective as shown in Proposition \ref{exactseq1}. These maps are the same at the level of the K-theory, through the Morita equivalence. Therefore the map at the utmost right on the bottom line is injective, and the map on the right is $0$. Assume then that $F$ is trivial. We have a sequence of morphisms $$ C(H) \xrightarrow{\iota_\kappa} C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}) \rightarrow C(\mathbb{G}) \xrightarrow{\pi_H} C(H),$$ where $\pi_H$ is defined in Remark \ref{RmkFwp}. The composition is equal to ${\rm id}_H$. Therefore, at the K-theoretic level, we have that the maps $K_0(C(H))\rightarrow K_0(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G}))$ must be injective, and that is enough to show that the map on the left side is $0$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
If $F$ is trivial then:
$$ K_1(C(\mathbb{G})) \simeq K_1(C(H))\oplus \bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^K K_1(B\otimes C(G))\simeq K_1(C(H))\oplus K_1(C(G))^{\oplus K^2}. $$
and,
$$K_0(C(\mathbb{G}))\simeq \bigoplus_{\kappa=1}^K K_0(C_\kappa(\mathbb{G})) / < \iota_{\gamma\ast}(h) - \iota_{\kappa\ast}(h) >, $$
for all $1\leq \kappa,\gamma\leq K$, and $g\in K_0(C(H))$.
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\cite{Vo17}
Let $(B,\psi)$ be a finite dimensional C*-algebra with a $\delta$-form. The CQG $H={\rm Aut}^+(B,\psi)$ is K-amenable and the K-theory groups of $C_\bullet(H)$ are
$$ K_0(C_\bullet(H))\simeq \mathbb{Z}^{K^2-2K+2} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_d^{2K-1}, $$
where $d$ is the gcd of the sizes of the blocks and $K$ their number, and
$$ K_1(C_\bullet(H))\simeq \mathbb{Z}.$$
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
If $H= {\rm Aut}^+(M_N(\mathbb{C}),\psi)$ then the class $[\beta(e_{11})]$ generates the free part of $K_0(C(H))$. That is to say $\mathbb{Z} \simeq \langle[\beta(e_{11})]\rangle \subset K_0(C(H)) \simeq \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_N$ is a direct factor.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
We use the counit $\varepsilon_H$ which is a unital $*$-morphism from $C(H)$ to $\mathbb{C}$. We have that $({\rm id}\otimes \varepsilon_H)\beta = {\rm id}$. Therefore the map $\varepsilon_{H\ast}$ is a left-inverse to the map $\beta_\ast$. Hence: $$ \mathbb{Z} \simeq K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C}))\xrightarrow{\beta_\ast} K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H))\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_\ast} K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}, $$ with the composition being the identity morphism. This implies that $[\beta(e_{11})]= \beta_\ast ([e_{11}])$ generates a direct factor.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{thmEtxt}
For $s,N\in \mathbb{N}$, and any faithful state $\psi\in M_N(\mathbb{C})^*$, the compact quantum group $\mathbb{G} :=\mathbb{Z}_s \wr_{*} {\rm Aut}^+(M_N(\mathbb{C}),\psi)$ is K-amenable and the K-theory groups of $C_\bullet(\mathbb{G})$ are:
$$K_0(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}^{s}\oplus \mathbb{Z}_N\quad\text{and}\quad K_1(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}.$$
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
In the case $B= M_N(\mathbb{C})$, we have the isomorphism $M_N(\mathbb{C}) \otimes C(\mathbb{G}) \simeq C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$. Therefore we can compute the K-theory groups of $C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}})$ only. The K-theory groups of $C(\mathbb{Z}_s)\simeq \mathbb{C}^s$ are 
$$
    K_0(\mathbb{C}^s)\simeq \mathbb{Z}^{s}\quad\text{and}\quad
    K_1(\mathbb{C}^s)\simeq 0.
$$
A basis of generators for $K_0(\mathbb{C}^s)\simeq \mathbb{Z}^{s}$ is the classes $[e_i]$ for $1\leq i\leq s$ but we remark that we can replace the last generator by the class $[1]= \sum_{i=1}^s [e_i]$, so that $\mathbb{Z}\cdot [1]$ is a direct factor in it. We immediately have that
$$K_1(C(\mathbb{G}))\simeq K_1(C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))\simeq K_1(M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H))\simeq \mathbb{Z}.$$
For the $K_0$ group we use the exact sequence
\begin{align*}
    0\rightarrow K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C})) \rightarrow K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(\mathbb{Z}_s))\oplus K_0(M_N(\mathbb{C})\otimes C(H)) \rightarrow K_0(C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))\rightarrow 0.
\end{align*}
This gives the isomorphism $$ K_0(C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}^s\oplus \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_N / \langle [1]-[\beta(e_{11})] \rangle. $$
By the previous discussions on the generators, we know that $\mathbb{Z}[1]$ and $\mathbb{Z}[\beta(e_{11})]$ are direct factors, and therefore we get that $K_0(C(\mathbb{G}))\simeq K_0(C(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}^s \oplus \mathbb{Z}_N$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
For $t,N\in \mathbb{N}$, the compact quantum group $\mathbb{G} :=\widehat{\mathbb{F}_t} \wr_{*} {\rm Aut}^+(M_N(\mathbb{C}),\psi)$ is K-amenable and the K-theory groups of $C_\bullet(\mathbb{G})$ are 
$$
    K_0(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}\oplus \mathbb{Z}_N\quad\text{and}\quad
    K_1(C_\bullet(\mathbb{G}))\simeq \mathbb{Z}^{t+1}.
$$
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
The proof is exactly the same as the previous case. Using that:
\begin{align*}
    K_0(C^\ast\mathbb{F}_t)&\simeq \mathbb{Z}, \text{ the generator being } [1],\\
    K_1(C^\ast\mathbb{F}_t)&\simeq \mathbb{Z}^t.
\end{align*}
We get that the two copies of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $K_0$ are identified, and the result.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
